name: public-apis
description: A collective list of free APIs
summary:
The Public APIs repository is a community-managed directory that curates an extensive collection of free and public APIs across diverse categories, intended for developers building modern applications and products. Maintained alongside APILayer, the repository catalogs APIs spanning domains such as animals, anime, anti-malware, blockchain, books, business, finance, geocoding, machine learning, security, transportation, and weather.

Key features include structured listings documenting API descriptions, authentication requirements (such as API keys, OAuth, or none), HTTPS support, and CORS availability. The repository also indexes Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, enabling AI agents and clients (e.g., Claude, Cursor, VS Code) to consume APIs directly as tools via standard transports like `stdio` and `HTTP`. Additionally, it highlights APILayer's suite of commercial REST services—such as IPstack, Marketstack, Fixer, and Aviationstack—accessible through Postman collections. Distributed under the MIT license, the project functions as a central lookup and discovery resource for third-party web services and data integrations.

name: free-programming-books
description: :books: Freely available programming books
summary:
Free Programming Books is a community-driven repository administered by the Free Ebook Foundation, a non-profit organization dedicated to the creation, distribution, archiving, and sustainability of free ebooks. Originally derived from a StackOverflow compilation, the project curates an extensive collection of freely available educational materials for software development and computer science across dozens of world languages.

Key capabilities and curated resource categories include:
- Books organized by programming language, subject, and multiple non-English languages.
- Cheat sheets across various topics.
- Free online courses translated and categorized by language.
- Interactive programming tutorials and web-based programming playgrounds for writing, compiling, and executing code in the browser.
- Problem sets and resources for competitive programming.
- Free podcasts and screencasts.

The collection can be browsed directly via repository Markdown files, viewed on a dedicated static website, or queried using an online dynamic search tool. The project serves learners, software developers, and educators worldwide, relying on open-source community contributions licensed under CC BY 4.0.

name: coding-interview-university
description: A complete computer science study plan to become a software engineer.
summary:
Coding Interview University is a structured, multi-month self-study plan designed to prepare developers for software engineering technical interviews at large technology companies such as Amazon, Google, Meta, and Microsoft. It caters to aspiring software engineers, especially self-taught developers without a formal computer science degree, who already possess basic programming knowledge. 

The study plan outlines an extensive curriculum that covers:
- Algorithmic complexity, Big-O notation, and asymptotic analysis
- Fundamental data structures: arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, hash tables, binary search trees, and heaps
- Essential algorithms: sorting methods (mergesort, quicksort, heapsort), graph algorithms (BFS, DFS, Dijkstra's algorithm, minimum spanning trees), binary search, and bit manipulation
- Core computer science topics: recursion, dynamic programming, system design, concurrency, processes and threads, memory hierarchy

name: awesome-python
description: The definitive list that answers "I want to do X in Python, which tool should I use?"
summary:
Awesome Python is an opinionated, curated index and directory of Python frameworks, libraries, tools, and learning resources. Aimed at Python developers and software engineers, it categorizes high-quality packages across numerous programming and system domains to facilitate software discovery and tech stack selection. 

The repository indexes tools across areas including AI, LLM agents, deep learning, machine learning, natural language processing, and computer vision. It covers web development (frameworks, APIs, servers, WebSockets, ORMs), data management (databases, caching, ETL pipelines, analytics, visualization), and software engineering workflows (testing, debugging, code analysis, packaging, task runners). Additional categories cover DevOps, distributed systems, CLI/GUI design, file/media manipulation, system security, penetration testing, and Python language runtimes. 

Featured technologies include popular libraries and tools such as Django, Flask, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Celery, Polars, Pydantic, uv, and Ruff. The project also links to an accompanying searchable web interface, as well as community newsletters, podcasts, and developer documentation guides.

name: awesome-selfhosted
description: A list of Free Software network services and web applications which can be hosted on your own servers
summary:
Awesome-Selfhosted is a curated list of Free Software network services and web applications that users can host and manage on their own servers rather than relying on Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) providers. It is designed for system administrators, homelab enthusiasts, developers, and privacy-conscious users seeking self-hosted alternatives to commercial platforms.

The repository indexes software across dozens of categories, including analytics, archiving, automation, booking, communication (email, IRC, SIP, video conferencing, XMPP), content management systems (CMS), databases, document management, e-commerce, feed readers, file sharing, gaming servers, generative AI, IoT, personal dashboards, and development tools. 

Each entry typically includes a description, license type (such as GPL, MIT, Apache-2.0, or AGPL-3.0), deployment formats (notably Docker, Kubernetes, deb packages), and core implementation languages (including Go, Python, Node.js, Rust, PHP, Java, C++, and Ruby). The list also flags anti-features when a self-hosted project depends on external proprietary services.

name: superpowers
description: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.
summary:
Superpowers is a software development methodology and skill framework designed for autonomous coding agents. It provides a structured workflow governed by composable, auto-triggering skills that guide agents through systematic engineering practices instead of jumping directly into writing code.

The core workflow enforces Socratic brainstorming to refine specifications, isolated workspace creation via Git worktrees, and detailed implementation planning emphasizing YAGNI, DRY, and Red-Green-Refactor test-driven development (TDD). Agents execute plans either through subagent-driven development (dispatching fresh review-gated subagents per bite-sized task) or inline execution. Additional skills govern systematic debugging, pre- and post-code reviews, branch finalization (merges and PRs), and session diagnostics via transcript analysis.

Superpowers is built for software developers utilizing AI coding assistants. It integrates across numerous harnesses, including Claude Code, Codex App and CLI, Cursor, Devin CLI, Factory Droid, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Grok Build CLI, Hermes Agent, Kimi Code, Muse, OpenCode, Pi, and Qwen Code.

name: 996.ICU
description: Repo for counting stars and contributing. Press F to pay respect to glorious developers.
summary:
996.ICU is an initiative started by IT practitioners to protest the "996" work schedule (9 a.m. to 9 p.m., 6 days per week, exceeding 60 hours weekly) and advocate for workers' legitimate rights and labor law compliance. The project's name stems from the ironic Chinese developer phrase, "Work by '996', sick in ICU."

The repository coordinates community-driven efforts to document labor conditions and support developers. Key capabilities include maintaining an evidence-backed blacklist of companies enforcing excessive overtime, collecting community proposals, and facilitating translations. It introduces the Anti-996 License, a software license adapted from the MIT license designed to be compatible with major open-source licenses while prohibiting companies that violate labor laws from utilizing the licensed code. 

Intended for software developers, IT workers, and community supporters globally, the initiative connects to various related community projects, such as company whitelists (955.WLB), ranking repositories, petitions, and blockchain-based evidence archives.

name: the-book-of-secret-knowledge
description: A collection of inspiring lists, manuals, cheatsheets, blogs, hacks, one-liners, cli/web tools and more.
summary:
"The Book of Secret Knowledge" is a curated reference collection of lists, manuals, cheatsheets, blogs, hacks, one-liners, and security resources. Aimed primarily at system and network administrators, DevOps engineers, penetration testers, and security researchers, the repository aggregates practical tools and educational materials across IT infrastructure and cybersecurity domains.

Key content areas and capabilities include:
- **CLI, GUI, and Web Tools**: Categorized utilities for shells, terminal multiplexers, network scanning, packet analysis, debugging, log parsing, SSL testing, and OSINT mass scanners.
- **Systems, Networks, and Containers**: Resources for Unix/BSD administration, Docker, Kubernetes orchestration, DNS/HTTP services, and operating system hardening.
- **Security and Penetration Testing**: Tool repositories, vulnerability databases (CVE/exploits), practice CTF labs, bug bounty frameworks, wordlists, and web app security guides.
- **Reference Materials & Cheatsheets**: Guides for building custom DNS/CAs, browser privacy extensions, and an extensive collection of practical shell one-liners and functions (utilizing tools such as OpenSSL, sed, awk, grep, tcpdump, nmap, and curl).

The repository serves as a centralized lookup handbook for day-to-day administration, security testing, and troubleshooting workflows.

name: deepseek-harness
description: DeepSeek Harness: Everything is a Plugin.
summary: DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) is an open-source agent harness developed by DeepSeek AI. It is built on an everything-is-a-plugin architecture powered by Cordis, utilizing the spatiotemporal composability programming paradigm. The project provides a Web UI for local and SSH execution modes. Technologies used include Node.js, TypeScript, and pnpm.

name: Python
description: All Algorithms implemented in Python
summary: TheAlgorithms - Python is an open-source repository containing a comprehensive collection of algorithms implemented in Python exclusively for educational and learning purposes. The project provides reference implementations that help users understand how various algorithms work, though they may be less efficient than those found in the Python standard library. Intended for students, developers, and programming enthusiasts looking to study core computer science concepts, the repository welcomes community contributions and offers structured navigation through a dedicated directory. Notable tooling and technologies associated with the project include Python, pre-commit, and ruff for code formatting.

name: andrej-karpathy-skills
description: A single CLAUDE.md file to improve Claude Code behavior, derived from Andrej Karpathy's observations on LLM coding pitfalls.
summary:
Karpathy-Inspired Claude Code Guidelines is a project providing a single `CLAUDE.md` configuration file and Claude Code plugin designed to improve Claude Code behavior by mitigating LLM coding pitfalls such as wrong assumptions, overcomplication, and unintended side effects. 

The project centers on four core principles: Think Before Coding, Simplicity First, Surgical Changes, and Goal-Driven Execution. It is intended for developers using AI coding assistants like Claude Code and Cursor to enforce disciplined, verifiable, and minimal code generation. Notable technologies mentioned include Claude Code, Cursor, and TypeScript.

name: vue
description: This is the repo for Vue 2. For Vue 3, go to https://github.com/vuejs/core
summary: Vue 2 is a progressive JavaScript framework designed for building user interfaces and scalable Single-Page Applications. It features an incrementally adoptable core library focused on the view layer, supporting browser environments compliant with ES5. The ecosystem includes libraries and tools such as `vue-router` for routing, `vuex` for state management, `vue-cli` for scaffolding, `vue-loader` for Single File Components with webpack, `vue-server-renderer` for server-side rendering, `vue-class-component` for TypeScript class-based APIs, `vue-rx` for RxJS integration, and `vue-devtools` for browser debugging. Vue 2 reached its End of Life on December 31, 2023, and no longer receives new features or updates.

name: opencode
description: The open source coding agent.
summary:
OpenCode is an open-source AI coding agent and desktop application designed to assist developers with development tasks, code exploration, and analysis. It provides built-in specialized agents, including a default full-access "build" agent, a read-only "plan" agent that restricts file edits and prompts for bash command permissions, and a general subagent for complex searches and multistep tasks. Users can switch between agents interactively using the Tab key or invoke the general subagent via `@general`. 

The project supports installation across multiple platforms via a shell script, npm, bun, pnpm, yarn, Homebrew, Scoop, Chocolatey, Pacman, AUR, mise, and Nix, alongside a desktop application available for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

name: computer-science
description: 🎓 Path to a free self-taught education in Computer Science!
summary:
Open Source Society University (OSSU) provides a comprehensive, free, self-taught undergraduate-level education in Computer Science using high-quality online courses and open materials primarily sourced from institutions like Harvard, Princeton, and MIT. 

The project is designed for self-motivated individuals seeking a well-rounded grounding in fundamental computing concepts without general education requirements. The curriculum spans introductory topics, a rigorous Core CS equivalent to the first three years of an undergraduate major (covering programming, math, tools, systems, theory, security, applications, and ethics), an Advanced CS section for specialized electives, and a culminating Final Project. It utilizes top-tier global coursework and textbooks aligned with the CS 2013 curriculum guidelines.

Intended users are dedicated learners worldwide with strong habits who want to master computer science independently or with peer support via the project's Discord community and GitHub. Notable technologies, languages, and tools referenced across the curriculum include Python, Standard ML, Racket, Ruby, C, C++, Java, Scala, Haskell, Prolog, Git, Vim, and Unix shells.

name: n8n
description: Fair-code workflow automation platform with native AI capabilities. Combine visual building with custom code, self-host or cloud, 400+ integrations.
summary:
n8n is a fair-code platform designed to build and deploy AI agents and workflow automation from prototype to production. It combines a visual canvas with custom code capabilities, supporting JavaScript, Python, and npm packages. 

Main capabilities include AI-native automation, model flexibility without vendor lock-in to connect with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or open-source models, tool use, human approvals, and full observability. The platform provides over 1,500 integrations and 9,000 workflow templates to connect AI with existing systems. It is targeted at users seeking to automate workflows and deploy AI agents, offering self-hosted deployment options with enterprise features such as role-based access and audit trails, as well as a cloud-based option. Built on Node.js, n8n supports Docker-based installations and is distributed under the Sustainable Use License and n8n Enterprise License.

name: FreeDomain
description: Free domain registration and practical DNS learning resources for everyone.
summary:
DigitalPlat FreeDomain is a public platform and learning resource offering free domain registration and DNS education. Aimed at making the web more accessible regardless of budget, the project enables users to register domains, connect preferred DNS providers via custom nameservers, and utilize comprehensive learning guides covering setup, DNS, website deployment, email, and operations. 

Supported domain extensions include .DPDNS.ORG, .US.KG, .QZZ.IO, .XX.KG, and .QD.JE. Designed and maintained by Edward Hsing of the DigitalPlat Foundation, the platform has registered over 500,000 domains. This repository houses public information, documentation, and learning resources, while the core application source code is maintained separately in the DigitalPlatDev/Domain-OSS repository. Community support is provided via an official Discord server and GitHub Discussions.

name: tensorflow
description: An Open Source Machine Learning Framework for Everyone
summary:
TensorFlow is an end-to-end open-source platform for machine learning, originally developed by researchers and engineers on the Google Brain team. It provides a comprehensive and flexible ecosystem of tools, libraries, and community resources designed to help researchers push state-of-the-art machine learning and neural network research, while enabling developers to build and deploy machine learning-powered applications. 

The intended users include researchers, developers, and data scientists. Notable capabilities include support for training and deploying models across multiple devices and platforms such as Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, and Raspberry Pi, with hardware acceleration options including CUDA-enabled GPUs, DirectX, and MacOS-metal. 

TensorFlow primarily provides stable APIs for Python and C++, alongside a non-guaranteed backward compatible API for other languages. Additional associated technologies and components mentioned include TensorBoard, LiteRT, XLA, pip, and Docker.

name: javascript-algorithms
description: 📝 Algorithms and data structures implemented in JavaScript with explanations and links to further readings
summary:
This repository provides JavaScript-based examples of popular algorithms and data structures, designed to help developers learn fundamental computer science concepts. Each data structure and algorithm features a dedicated README with explanations, complexity charts, and further reading links.

**Main Capabilities & Technologies:**
* **Data Structures:** Implements linked lists, doubly linked lists, queues, stacks, deques, hash tables, heaps, priority queues, tries, various trees (Binary Search, AVL, Red-Black, Segment, Fenwick), graphs, disjoint sets, Bloom filters, and LRU caches.
* **Algorithms:** Covers mathematical computations, set manipulations, string searching and matching (such as KMP, Rabin-Karp, Levenshtein distance), searching, sorting, graph traversal (DFS, BFS, Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall), cryptography ciphers, and machine learning basics (k-NN, k-Means).
* **Paradigms:** Demonstrates solutions utilizing brute force, greedy, divide and conquer, dynamic programming, backtracking, and branch and bound techniques.
* **Tooling:** Built with JavaScript (Node.js >=16), utilizing npm for package management, ESLint for code quality checks, and Jest for running test suites. 

**Intended Users:** 
Developers, students, and software engineers looking to study, practice, or review data structures and algorithms using JavaScript implementations.

name: yt-dlp
description: A feature-rich command-line audio/video downloader
summary:
yt-dlp is a feature-rich, command-line audio and video downloader supporting thousands of websites. It is a fork of youtube-dl based on the inactive youtube-dlc project. 

Main capabilities include downloading single videos and playlists, format selection and sorting, extracting and embedding subtitles, thumbnails, and metadata, splitting or downloading specific sections of videos, integrating with the SponsorBlock API, and updating itself across different release channels (`stable`, `nightly`, and `master`). It also supports plugins, browser cookie extraction, and various post-processing tasks.

Intended users range from regular users seeking an easy-to-use multimedia downloader to developers looking to embed video extraction capabilities into Python applications.

Notable technologies used include Python (3.10+ / 3.11+ PyPy), FFmpeg and ffprobe for media processing, PyInstaller for building standalone executables, and optional runtime engines such as Deno, Node.js, Bun, or QuickJS alongside packages like certifi, brotli, websockets, requests, and curl_cffi.

name: claw-code
description: An agent-managed museum exhibit, built in Rust with Gajae-Code / LazyCodex — developed and maintained with no human intervention.
summary:
Claw Code (ultraworkers/claw-code) is an agent-managed exhibit and the public Rust implementation of the `claw` CLI agent harness, designed to plan, execute, verify, label, and preserve artifacts. 

**Main Capabilities:**
- Provides the `claw` command-line interface for running prompts and managing interactive agent sessions.
- Includes a health-check tool (`claw doctor`) to validate API keys, model access, and tool configurations.
- Supports integration with local OpenAI-compatible providers, offline skill installations, and customizable task workflows.
- Contains companion workspaces, parity harnesses, and structured documentation for configuration and building.

**Intended Users:**
Developers and contributors experimenting with agent harnesses, local AI models, and autonomous command-line agent workflows.

**Notable Technologies:**
- **Rust** (Workspace and CLI binary implementation)
- **PowerShell** / **Git Bash** / **WSL** (Cross-platform shell environments)
- **Anthropic API** and **OpenAI-compatible APIs** (such as Ollama, llama.cpp, and vLLM)

name: vscode
description: Visual Studio Code
summary: The `Code - OSS` repository is the open-source project by Microsoft used to develop Visual Studio Code in collaboration with the community under the MIT license. It combines the simplicity of a code editor with tools for the edit-build-debug cycle, offering comprehensive code editing, navigation, understanding, lightweight debugging, a rich extensibility model, and integration with existing tools. Intended for developers, the platform supports Windows, macOS, and Linux, and includes built-in extensions and language features. Notable technologies and integration features mentioned include Docker, Dev Containers, and GitHub Codespaces.

name: Microsoft-Activation-Scripts
description: Open-source Windows and Office activator featuring HWID, Ohook, TSforge, and Online KMS activation methods, along with advanced troubleshooting.
summary:
Microsoft Activation Scripts (MAS) is an open-source Windows and Office activator designed to activate Windows (including Windows 8.1, 10, and 11), Office, and Extended Security Updates (ESU). 

The project features multiple activation methods, including HWID, Ohook, TSforge, and Online KMS, alongside advanced troubleshooting capabilities. It is intended for users seeking to activate Microsoft products on Windows Vista and later operating systems. 

Execution is supported through PowerShell scripts—using `irm` and `iex` commands with optional DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) support to bypass ISP or DNS blocking—as well as through a traditional batch script (`MAS_AIO.cmd`) or downloaded ZIP archive.

name: ohmyzsh
description: 🙃   A delightful community-driven (with 2,500+ contributors) framework for managing your zsh configuration. Includes 300+ optional plugins (rails, git, macOS, hub, docker, homebrew, node, php, python, etc), 140+ themes to spice up your morning, and an auto-update tool that makes it easy to keep up with the latest updates from the community.
summary:
Oh My Zsh is an open-source, community-driven framework designed for managing Zsh configurations. It aims to enhance the terminal shell experience for developers and system administrators by providing hundreds of powerful plugins and customizable themes. 

Key capabilities include plugin and theme management, automatic update configurations, support for custom plugins and themes, an async git prompt feature, and command-line tools for manual or automated updates and uninstallation. Operating system compatibility includes Android, FreeBSD, Linux, macOS, and Windows via WSL2. 

Notable technologies and tools utilized by the framework include Zsh, Git, curl, and wget.

name: firecrawl
description: Supercharge your AI agents with data from the web and beyond. Building the library for superintelligence. 🔥
summary:
Firecrawl is an open-source web data extraction platform and library designed to supercharge AI agents and developers with clean, LLM-ready web data. It enables users to convert URLs into markdown, HTML, screenshots, or structured JSON, search the web, crawl entire websites, map domains, batch-scrape URLs, and perform autonomous data gathering using AI agents and interactive prompts. 

Main capabilities include handling JavaScript-heavy pages, rotating proxies, rate limits, media parsing (PDFs, DOCX), and element interaction (clicking, scrolling, waiting). The project provides official SDKs for Python, Node.js, Go, Java, Elixir, Rust, Ruby, .NET, and PHP, alongside a CLI, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and integrations with tools like Zapier, n8n, and Lovable. It is intended for developers, AI agent builders, and researchers requiring reliable, real-time web scraping and data aggregation. Firecrawl is licensed under the AGPL-3.0 (with SDKs under the MIT License) and is available both as an open-source project for self-hosting and as a hosted service at firecrawl.dev.

name: markitdown
description: Python tool for converting files and office documents to Markdown.
summary:
MarkItDown is a lightweight Python utility designed to convert various file formats into Markdown for use with Large Language Models (LLMs) and text analysis pipelines. It prioritizes preserving document structure—such as headings, lists, tables, and links—over high-fidelity human presentation. 

Supported formats include PDF, PowerPoint, Word, Excel, images, audio, HTML, text-based formats (CSV, JSON, XML), ZIP archives, YouTube URLs, and EPubs. The project also provides optional integrations for Azure Document Intelligence and Azure Content Understanding, supports third-party plugins (such as `markitdown-ocr`), and offers a command-line interface, a Docker image, and a Python API. 

Intended for developers incorporating file conversion libraries into larger systems rather than end-user applications like web servers or graphical user interfaces, MarkItDown requires Python 3.10 through 3.14 and utilizes Hatch for development. Notable technologies and integrations include OpenAI clients for image description and transcription, Azure AI services, and `uv` or Anaconda for environment management.

name: AutoGPT
description: AutoGPT is the vision of accessible AI for everyone, to use and to build on. Our mission is to provide the tools, so that you can focus on what matters.
summary:
AutoGPT is an open-source platform designed to build, deploy, and run AI agents that automate multi-step workflows. It features a visual builder and conversational interface (AutoPilot) to create custom agents, a dashboard to monitor executions and costs, and a marketplace for community-built agents. The platform automates tasks across executive operations, sales, marketing, engineering, customer support, and research.

Intended users include developers, business professionals, and teams looking to automate repetitive tasks or build custom AI workflows without extensive coding. 

Notable technologies and integrations include Docker, hundreds of AI models, and over 45 connected platforms such as Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Docs, Google Sheets, GitHub, Slack, Discord, Notion, HubSpot, Linear, Airtable, Jira, Salesforce, Stripe, and Webflow. The project offers a managed hosted platform as well as a self-hosted deployment option using Docker containers on Linux and macOS. Licensing includes the Polyform Shield license for `autogpt_platform/` and the MIT License for `classic/` and other components.

name: Python-100-Days
description: Python - 100天从新手到大师
summary:
The repository is a comprehensive, 100-day Python learning guide created by 骆昊 (Luo Hao) designed to take learners from novice to master. The project covers Python language basics, advanced application development, web development with Django, network data scraping, data analysis, machine learning, and team project development. 

**Main Capabilities:**
- Structured daily learning path spanning 100 days across multiple domains, including language foundations, file handling, relational databases (MySQL, Hive), web frameworks, and APIs.
- Comprehensive modules for data science and visualization using libraries like NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Pyecharts.
- Machine learning and AI application tutorials covering algorithms such as kNN, decision trees, random forests, regression, clustering, neural networks, and natural language processing.
- Software engineering best practices including unit testing, Docker containerization, performance optimization, and team collaboration workflows.

**Intended Users:**
Beginners, students, professionals, and developers looking to systematically learn Python, transition into fields like data science, web development, or machine learning, or prepare for technical interviews.

**Notable Technologies:**
Python, Django, Django REST Framework (DRF), MySQL, Hive, Redis, Docker, Kubernetes, Celery, NumPy, Pandas, Scrapy, Selenium, Pytest, Git, Nginx.

name: awesome-go
description: A curated list of awesome Go frameworks, libraries and software
summary:
Awesome Go is a curated, community-driven list of Go frameworks, libraries, software, and resources. It serves as a comprehensive directory for developers working with the Go programming language, cataloging tools across dozens of technical domains including artificial intelligence, blockchain, web development, databases, cryptography, stream processing, networking, and machine learning. 

The repository indexes thousands of packages categorized into structured topics such as command-line interfaces, continuous integration, configuration management, concurrency primitives (goroutines), database drivers, GUI development, and testing frameworks. In addition to software libraries, Awesome Go points developers toward learning materials like e-books, style guides, community meetups, and interactive tutorials. 

Designed primarily for Go developers, system architects, and software engineers seeking vetted packages and architectural patterns, the project promotes open-source ecosystem discovery. It relies on community contributions via GitHub pull requests to maintain relevance and currency. Notable technologies referenced throughout the ecosystem include standard Go concurrency models, WebAssembly, gRPC, Protocol Buffers, and cloud-native infrastructure components like Kubernetes and Docker.

name: CS-Notes
description: :books: 技术面试必备基础知识、Leetcode、计算机操作系统、计算机网络、系统设计
summary:
CS-Notes is a comprehensive technical learning repository and interview preparation guide designed for computer science students and software engineers. It provides structured notes, algorithm solutions, and reference materials covering core computer science subjects. 

Main capabilities and topics include:
- **Algorithms:** LeetCode solutions, Sword to Offer (剑指 Offer) solutions, and general algorithmic concepts.
- **Computer Science Fundamentals:** Operating Systems, Linux, Computer Networks, HTTP, and Socket programming.
- **Databases:** Database system principles, SQL syntax and exercises, MySQL, and Redis.
- **Java Ecosystem:** Java basics, containers, concurrency, Java Virtual Machine (JVM), and Java I/O.
- **System Design:** Distributed systems, clustering, caching, message queues, and security/attack techniques.
- **Object-Oriented Programming:** Object-oriented paradigms and design patterns.
- **Development Tools & Practices:** Git, Docker, build tools, regular expressions, code readability, and coding style guidelines.

name: You-Dont-Know-JS
description: A book series (2 published editions) on the JS language.
summary: "You Don't Know JS Yet" (2nd Edition) is a book series by Kyle Simpson that dives deep into the core mechanisms of the JavaScript language. The repository contains the online texts for the second edition, which includes titles such as "Get Started", "Scope & Closures", and "The Unbooks" (incorporating drafts for "Objects & Classes" and "Types & Grammar"). The project is intended for developers seeking a comprehensive understanding of JavaScript fundamentals. The content is self-published through GetiPub and licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs 4.0 Unported License.

name: ollama
description: Get up and running with Kimi, GLM, MiniMax, DeepSeek, gpt-oss, Qwen, Gemma and other models.
summary: Ollama is a tool designed to help users easily download, run, and manage open large language models locally. It provides a command-line interface, a REST API, and native libraries for Python and JavaScript, enabling developers to integrate open models into custom applications, agents, or existing IDEs and coding assistants like Claude Code, Codex, and Copilot. Intended for developers, researchers, and general users looking to run AI models on personal hardware, Ollama supports backends such as `llama.cpp` and offers extensive integrations with chat interfaces, code editors, RAG pipelines, and infrastructure tools across macOS, Windows, Linux, and Docker environments.

name: HelloGitHub
description: :octocat: 分享 GitHub 上有趣、入门级的开源项目。Share interesting, entry-level open source projects on GitHub.
summary: HelloGitHub is a curated publication and resource sharing project designed to introduce interesting, beginner-friendly open-source software. Published monthly on the 28th, the project features hand-picked open-source projects, technical books, practical applications, and enterprise-grade repositories to help developers and enthusiasts discover the appeal of open source. Intended for users looking to explore and learn about open-source technologies, HelloGitHub provides structured issues and selections accessible via its official website and community channels.

name: skills
description: Public repository for Agent Skills
summary:
This repository contains Anthropic's implementation of Agent Skills for Claude, serving as a demonstration and educational resource for the Agent Skills standard. Skills are self-contained folders comprising instructions, scripts, and resources (`SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter) that Claude loads dynamically to improve repeatable performance on specialized tasks. 

The project purpose is to showcase patterns and approaches for teaching Claude specific workflows. Main capabilities span creative and design applications, technical tasks such as web app testing and MCP server generation, enterprise communication, branding, and document creation and editing (specifically supporting docx, pdf, pptx, and xlsx formats). 

Intended users are developers, prompt engineers, and enterprises looking to build, reference, or use custom skills via Claude Code, Claude.ai, or the Claude API. Notable technologies include Claude Code, the Claude API, Markdown, and YAML.

name: flutter
description: Flutter makes it easy and fast to build beautiful apps for mobile and beyond
summary:
Flutter is Google's free, open-source software development kit (SDK) designed for crafting user experiences across mobile, web, and desktop from a single codebase. Intended for developers and designers targeting iOS, Android, web, Windows, macOS, Linux, or embedded platforms, Flutter utilizes a layered architecture for pixel-control and provides a comprehensive set of widgets including Cupertino and Material components. 

The project is powered by the Dart programming language, which compiles to 32-bit and 64-bit ARM machine code, JavaScript, WebAssembly, and Intel x64 and ARM for desktops. For performance, Flutter leverages hardware-accelerated 2D graphics libraries like Skia and Impeller to ensure native-speed graphics. It features stateful hot reload for productive development, supports FFI and platform channels for accessing native code, and integrates with development tools such as Visual Studio Code and IntelliJ or Android Studio via dedicated plug-ins.

name: gitignore
description: A collection of useful .gitignore templates
summary:
This repository contains GitHub’s official collection of `.gitignore` file templates, used to populate the `.gitignore` template choosers in the GitHub.com interface when creating new repositories and files. The project purpose is to provide curated sets of rules for Git repositories to prevent committing unimportant files associated with specific programming languages, frameworks, tools, editors, and operating systems. 

The folder structure organizes these resources into root templates for common mainstream technologies, a `Global` folder for editors, tools, and operating systems, and a `community` folder containing specialized and versioned templates for frameworks, older versions, and less mainstream tools. Intended users include developers and repository maintainers seeking to configure standard ignore rules for their projects. Technologies referenced include Git and various programming languages, frameworks, and development environments.

name: bootstrap
description: The most popular HTML, CSS, and JavaScript framework for developing responsive, mobile first projects on the web.
summary:
Bootstrap is a sleek, intuitive, and powerful front-end framework designed for faster and easier web development. Its primary purpose is to provide developers with pre-styled components, grid systems, and utilities to build responsive, mobile-first websites and web applications. 

Main capabilities include compiled and minified CSS and JavaScript distributions, source maps for debugging, and bundled JavaScript files incorporating Popper. The repository contains source code for grid frameworks, reboot resets, utilities, and components, alongside project documentation built with Astro and powered by Algolia's DocSearch. 

Intended users are web developers and front-end engineers seeking standardized styles and layouts. Notable technologies used within the project and its toolchain include HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Sass, Astro, Node.js, and Popper. Distributed via package managers like npm, Yarn, Bun, Composer, and NuGet, Bootstrap adheres to Semantic Versioning and is licensed under the MIT License.

name: prompts.chat
description: f.k.a. Awesome ChatGPT Prompts. Share, discover, and collect prompts from the community. Free and open source — self-host for your organization with complete privacy.
summary:
Prompts.chat (formerly known as Awesome ChatGPT Prompts) is an open-source prompt library and dataset designed for AI chat models such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, and Mistral. The project serves AI practitioners, developers, researchers, and educators by providing a curated collection of prompts for various use cases, an interactive book on prompt engineering, and a game-based prompting adventure for children. 

Main capabilities include browsing and contributing to prompts, self-hosting private prompt libraries with custom branding and authentication, and integrating via a CLI, Claude Code plugin, or Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Data formats are available as CSV and Hugging Face datasets. Notable technologies used in the project include PostgreSQL and Neon.

name: transformers
description: 🤗 Transformers: the model-definition framework for state-of-the-art machine learning models in text, vision, audio, and multimodal models, for both inference and training.
summary:
Transformers is a model-definition framework designed for state-of-the-art machine learning tasks spanning text, computer vision, audio, video, and multimodal applications. It supports both inference and training, acting as a central pivot across frameworks like PyTorch, JAX, and TensorFlow, as well as various training tools, inference engines, and adjacent modeling libraries. 

The library targets researchers, engineers, developers, students, and practitioners seeking to leverage or adapt pretrained model checkpoints. Key capabilities include high-performance natural language understanding and generation, automatic speech recognition, image classification, visual question answering, and text generation via high-level APIs like the Pipeline class. It provides hundreds of model architectures and access to over one million pretrained model checkpoints on the Hugging Face Hub. Notable technologies and frameworks referenced include PyTorch, Whisper, DINO v2, BLIP, Llama, Qwen, and DeepSpeed.

name: stable-diffusion-webui
description: Stable Diffusion web UI
summary:
Stable Diffusion web UI is a browser-based interface for Stable Diffusion implemented using the Gradio library. It provides a comprehensive suite of tools for image generation, editing, and model training. 

Main capabilities include standard txt2img and img2img modes, inpainting, outpainting, color sketching, prompt matrix generation, high-resolution fixes, and multidimensional X/Y/Z parameter plots. The platform supports advanced prompt engineering features such as attention weights, negative prompts, prompt editing mid-generation, and zero token limits using Composable Diffusion. It incorporates model training tools for Textual Inversion embeddings, hypernetworks, and LoRAs, alongside dataset preprocessing via BLIP and DeepDanbooru. Additionally, the interface features an Extras tab integrated with neural network upscalers and face restoration tools such as GFPGAN, CodeFormer, RealESRGAN, SwinIR, and LDSR.

The project is intended for AI artists, researchers, and developers running Stable Diffusion locally or via cloud services. It supports hardware acceleration technologies including NVidia CUDA, AMD ROCm, Apple Silicon, and xformers for performance optimization, running on Python.

name: the-art-of-command-line
description: Master the command line, in one page
summary:
The repository "The Art of Command Line" provides a comprehensive collection of notes and practical tips for mastering the Unix command line, primarily focusing on interactive Bash and Linux environments. Its purpose is to improve engineering productivity and flexibility through command-line fluency. 

The guide covers a wide range of topics suited for both beginners and experienced users, including basics, everyday use, file and data processing, system debugging, one-liners, and obscure yet useful utilities, alongside dedicated sections for macOS and Windows environments. Main capabilities include process and job management, text and data manipulation using tools like `awk`, `sed`, `jq`, and `grep`, system and network debugging via `strace`, `netstat`, `ss`, and `lsof`, file synchronization with `rsync`, and shell script hardening techniques. 

Notable technologies and tools referenced include Bash, Vim, Git, `jq`, `pandoc`, `tmux`, `ripgrep` (`rg`), `fzf`, `awk`, `sed`, Cygwin, and Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL). Intended users are software engineers, system administrators, and developers seeking to deepen their terminal expertise.

name: JavaGuide
description: Java 面试 & 后端通用面试指南，覆盖计算机基础、数据库、分布式、高并发、系统设计与 AI 应用开发
summary:
JavaGuide is a comprehensive knowledge repository and interview preparation guide designed for Java backend developers and computer science learners. The project's purpose is to systemize essential technical knowledge, core concepts, and high-frequency interview questions for technical career preparation. 

Main capabilities include structured learning roadmaps, in-depth source code analyses, and interview summaries spanning core Java (such as collections, concurrency, I/O, JVM, and new language features), computer science foundations (operating systems, computer networks, data structures, and algorithms), and major databases like MySQL, Redis, and MongoDB. It also covers development tools (Maven, Docker, Git), system design, distributed systems architecture (RPC, ZooKeeper, distributed locks, and transactions), and strategies for high-performance and high-availability engineering. 

The intended users are students, job seekers, and backend software engineers preparing for technical interviews or seeking to deepen their understanding of Java ecosystem principles. Notable technologies and frameworks referenced throughout the guide include Java, Spring, Spring Boot, MyBatis, Dubbo, Spring Cloud Gateway, Elasticsearch, and various messaging middleware systems such as Kafka, RocketMQ, and RabbitMQ.

name: dify
description: Build Agentic workflows, RAG pipelines, with rich AI model and tool support on one collaborative workspace. Deploy on cloud, VPC, or self-hosted, so teams move from prototype to production without rebuilding the stack.
summary:
Dify is an open-source Large Language Model (LLM) app development platform designed to take projects from prototype to production. It targets developers, organizations, and AI builders seeking an intuitive interface for creating AI applications. 

The platform's main capabilities include:
- **Visual AI Workflows:** Build and test workflows on a visual canvas.
- **Comprehensive Model Support:** Integrate proprietary and open-source models (such as GPT, Mistral, and Llama3) from various inference providers or self-hosted setups via OpenAI API-compatible options.
- **Prompt IDE:** Craft prompts, compare model performance, and incorporate features like text-to-speech.
- **RAG Pipeline:** Handle document ingestion, text extraction (from PDFs, PPTs, and common formats), and retrieval.
- **Autonomous Agents:** Build agents with sandboxes to run commands, install software, handle files, and connect tools via the Dify Marketplace, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, or custom APIs.
- **LLMOps & Backend-as-a-Service:** Monitor logs and application performance using integrations like Opik, Langfuse, and Arize Phoenix, while accessing corresponding APIs for integration into business logic.

Dify can be deployed via Docker Compose, used via Dify Cloud, or adopted as an enterprise solution.

name: agency-agents
description: A complete AI agency at your fingertips - From frontend wizards to Reddit community ninjas, from whimsy injectors to reality checkers. Each agent is a specialized expert with personality, processes, and proven deliverables.
summary:
The Agency is a collection of over 230 specialized, personality-driven AI agents organized across divisions including Engineering, Design, Paid Media, Sales, Marketing, Product, Project Management, Testing, Security, Support, Spatial Computing, Specialized, Finance, Game Development, Academic, GIS, Healthcare, and Research. 

The project purpose is to provide ready-to-use, production-grade AI specialist personalities—such as frontend developers, security architects, and growth hackers—that deliver concrete technical outputs, structured workflows, and measurable outcomes rather than generic prompt templates.

Intended users include developers, product teams, marketers, sales professionals, and organizations seeking multidisciplinary AI agent workflows. The repository provides a native desktop companion app (Agency Agents) for macOS, Linux, and Windows, alongside conversion and installation scripts supporting various developer environments and agent harnesses. Notable technologies and integrations mentioned include Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Aider, Windsurf, OpenClaw, Qwen Code, Kimi Code, Codex, Osaurus, Hermes, and DeepSeek Harness.

name: langflow
description: Langflow is a powerful tool for building and deploying AI-powered agents and workflows.
summary:
Langflow is a platform for building, orchestrating, and deploying AI-powered agents and workflows. Intended for developers, it provides a visual builder interface, an interactive playground with step-by-step control, and source code access allowing components to be customized using Python. The platform supports multi-agent orchestration, conversation management, retrieval, and enterprise-ready security and scalability. 

Main capabilities include deploying workflows as APIs or MCP servers, exporting flows as JSON for Python applications, and integrating observability tools such as LangSmith and LangFuse. Langflow supports major LLMs, vector databases, and a library of AI tools. Technologies utilized include Python (versions 3.10 to 3.14), uv, Docker, and an available Langflow Desktop application for Windows and macOS.

name: open-webui
description: User-friendly AI Interface (Supports Ollama, OpenAI API, ...)
summary:
Open WebUI is a self-hosted, feature-rich, and extensible AI platform designed to run entirely offline or connect to cloud providers. It provides a provider-agnostic user interface supporting local models via Ollama alongside OpenAI-compatible APIs such as LMStudio, GroqCloud, Mistral, OpenRouter, and vLLM. 

Main capabilities include granular Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), multi-model conversations, agentic execution with terminal environments, persistent memory, local and web-search-backed Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) across multiple vector databases, voice and video calling, calendar scheduling, image generation and editing via engines like DALL·E and ComfyUI, and usage analytics. It supports Markdown, LaTeX, and extensive extensibility through filters, actions, pipes, tools, and OpenAPI tool servers. 

Intended users include individuals, developer teams, and enterprises seeking a customizable, self-hosted AI interface with robust security, enterprise authentication (LDAP, SSO, SCIM 2.0), and horizontal scalability using Redis and OpenTelemetry. Notable technologies utilized include Docker, Kubernetes, Python, Ollama, Redis, PostgreSQL, and SQLite.

name: ponytail
description: Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
summary:
Ponytail is an AI agent plugin and ruleset designed to reduce over-engineering by guiding AI coding assistants to write minimal, necessary code without sacrificing safety, validation, error handling, security, or accessibility. 

### Project Purpose
The project aims to prevent AI agents from unnecessarily bloating codebases (such as installing heavy dependencies or writing wrapper components when native features, standard libraries, or existing codebase patterns suffice). It enforces a strict evaluation ladder: rejecting unnecessary code, reusing existing code, utilizing the standard library, platform features, or installed dependencies, and preferring one-line solutions before building new components.

### Main Capabilities
- **Reduced Output:** Consistently cuts lines of code, token usage, cost, and time compared to unassisted baselines while maintaining 100% safety.
- **Configurable Intensity Levels:** Supports modes including `lite`, `full`, `ultra`, and `off`.
- **Built-in Slash Commands:** Provides interactive commands such as `/ponytail` (mode switching and status), `/ponytail-review` (diff analysis for over-engineering), `/ponytail-audit` (repository-wide analysis), `/ponytail-debt` (tracking deferred shortcuts), and `/ponytail-gain` (benchmark impact scoreboard).
- **Multi-Platform Integrations:** Ships plugins, hooks, extensions, and rule files for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, OpenCode, Gemini, Antigravity, Qoder, Pi, Hermes Agent, CodeWhale, Swival, Devin, OpenClaw, Grok Build, Kiro, Junie, Amp, and Jules.

### Intended Users
Software developers and teams utilizing AI coding agents who want to minimize generated code volume, reduce API costs and latency, and prevent unnecessary dependency bloat.

### Notable Technologies
- Node.js (used for lifecycle hooks and build scripts)
- Support for various AI agent harnesses, IDE extensions, and CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, etc.)

name: scrcpy
description: Display and control your Android device
summary:
scrcpy is a free, open-source application designed to mirror and control Android devices (running Android 5.0 or above) from Linux, Windows, or macOS computers. Connected via USB or TCP/IP, it provides high performance with low latency (35–70ms) and high frame rates (30–120fps) without requiring root access or an app installed on the target device. 

Main capabilities include audio and video forwarding, screen recording, virtual displays, camera mirroring, webcam exposure via V4L2 (Linux-only), bidirectional copy-paste, OTG mode, and physical keyboard, mouse (HID), and gamepad simulation. Users can control devices with configurable quality settings, H.264/H.265 video codecs, and perform actions with zero ads or accounts required.

name: claude-code
description: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that lives in your terminal, understands your codebase, and helps you code faster by executing routine tasks, explaining complex code, and handling git workflows - all through natural language commands.
summary: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that operates in the terminal, IDE, or via GitHub tags (`@claude`), enabling developers to interact with their codebase using natural language commands. Its main capabilities include executing routine tasks, explaining complex code, handling git workflows, and extending functionality through custom commands and agents via included plugins. Designed for developers seeking to code faster, the project requires Node.js 18+ and is distributed through installation methods including shell scripts, Homebrew, and WinGet.

name: clash-verge-rev
description: A modern GUI client based on Tauri, designed to run in Windows, macOS and Linux for tailored proxy experience
summary:
Clash Verge Rev is a Clash Meta GUI desktop application built as a continuation of Clash Verge. Designed for users seeking a rule-based proxy tunnel manager, the software features a clean, customizable user interface with support for theme colors, tray icons, and CSS injection. 

Main capabilities include built-in Clash.Meta (mihomo) kernel support with Alpha version switching, profile management and enhancement via Merge and Script with syntax hints, system proxying, a TUN virtual network card mode, visual node and rule editing, and WebDAV configuration backup and synchronization. 

The project is built using Rust and the Tauri framework, alongside Vite for frontend tooling, and supports Windows, Linux, and macOS platforms. The application enforces a local-first privacy policy where configuration and logs remain exclusively on the user's device.

name: javascript
description: JavaScript Style Guide
summary:
The Airbnb JavaScript Style Guide provides a comprehensive, reasonable approach to writing JavaScript (ES6+) code. Its purpose is to establish consistent coding standards and best practices covering types, references, objects, arrays, destructuring, strings, functions, arrow functions, classes, modules, iterators, properties, variables, hoisting, comparisons, blocks, control statements, comments, whitespace, commas, semicolons, type coercion, naming conventions, accessors, events, jQuery usage, and the standard library.

The guide targets JavaScript developers and teams seeking to maintain clean, readable, and robust codebases. Notable technologies and tools referenced throughout include ECMAScript 6+ (ES2015+), Babel, babel-preset-airbnb, airbnb-browser-shims, ESLint (with configurations like eslint-config-airbnb and eslint-config-airbnb-base), JSHint, Webpack, Mocha, Jest, and Tape.

name: langchain
description: The agent engineering platform.
summary:
LangChain is a Python agent engineering framework and platform designed for building agents and LLM-powered applications by chaining together interoperable components, models, embeddings, vector stores, and third-party integrations. It provides a modular, component-based architecture featuring real-time data augmentation, model interoperability, and flexible abstraction layers. 

Intended for developers and engineering teams, the platform simplifies AI application development, rapid prototyping, and production deployment. It integrates within a broader ecosystem that includes LangGraph for controllable agent workflows, Deep Agents for built-in planning, subagents, and file system usage, and LangSmith for debugging, evaluation, monitoring, and deployments.

name: system-prompts-and-models-of-ai-tools
description: FULL Augment Code, Claude Code, Cluely, CodeBuddy, Comet, Cursor, Devin AI, Junie, Kiro, Leap.new, Lovable, Manus, NotionAI, Orchids.app, Perplexity, Poke, Qoder, Replit, Same.dev, Trae, Traycer AI, VSCode Agent, Warp.dev, Windsurf, Xcode, Z.ai Code, Dia & v0. (And other Open Sourced) System Prompts, Internal Tools & AI Models
summary: This repository provides a comprehensive collection of system prompts and models of various AI tools, curated to offer insights into their configuration and behavior. Targeted at developers, researchers, and AI startups, the project serves as a centralized resource for examining leaked or exposed AI system prompts and models while highlighting associated security risks such as prompt injection and system prompt extraction.

name: tech-interview-handbook
description: Curated coding interview preparation materials for busy software engineers
summary:
The Tech Interview Handbook is a free, curated collection of technical interview preparation materials designed for software engineers. The project provides practical content covering all interview phases, including job applications, coding interviews, behavioral questions, algorithm cheatsheets, study plans (such as Grind 75 and Blind 75), software engineer resume guides, and offer negotiation. 

Intended for individuals new to technical interviews, job seekers targeting top tech companies, and seasoned engineers looking to refresh their interview skills, the handbook focuses on direct, condensed content rather than external links. The repository's documentation and website are built using Docusaurus.

name: next.js
description: The React Framework
summary: Next.js is a framework that enables the creation of full-stack web applications by extending the latest React features and integrating Rust-based JavaScript tooling for fast builds. Developed by Vercel and used by large companies, it provides built-in documentation, a learning course, a showcase of built sites, and active community channels including GitHub Discussions and Discord.

name: youtube-dl
description: Command-line program to download videos from YouTube.com and other video sites
summary:
youtube-dl is a command-line program and Python library designed to download videos and extract media from YouTube.com and a wide variety of other video platforms. It supports platform-agnostic execution across Unix-based systems, Windows, and macOS, and requires the Python interpreter (versions 2.6, 2.7, or 3.2+). 

The software caters to end-users seeking versatile media downloading capabilities—such as format selection, playlist management, geo-restriction bypassing, subtitles extraction, authentication handling, and post-processing via FFmpeg—as well as developers wishing to embed video downloading features into Python applications or extend support to new platforms. Notable technological integrations include support for external downloaders like aria2c, curl, and wget, along with Python-based modular extractors and utilities like traverse_obj for safe metadata parsing.

name: awesome-llm-apps
description: 100+ AI Agents, Agent Skills and RAG Apps - Free and Open Source.
summary:
Awesome LLM Apps is a collection of over 100 open-source AI agents, agent skills, RAG applications, and multi-agent teams. Released under the Apache-2.0 license, the repository provides pre-built, end-to-end tested templates that work with various foundation models, including Claude, Gemini, GPT, DeepSeek, Llama, Qwen, and Grok. 

The project aims to help developers quickly build, run, and scale AI-powered workflows. Its extensive catalog includes agent skills, starter and advanced AI agents, always-on background agents, multi-agent teams, voice AI agents, generative UI apps, autonomous game-playing agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) tutorials, LLM optimization tools, and fine-tuning recipes for models like Gemma and Llama using Unsloth. Notable technologies and frameworks referenced across the repository include Streamlit, LangGraph, Qdrant, AG2, CrewAI, and the OpenAI Agents SDK. 

Intended for developers, AI engineers, and researchers, the repository supports quick setups via pip, npm, and Docker, enabling users to deploy autonomous workflows, local offline RAG pipelines, and interactive AI applications effortlessly.

name: iptv
description: Collection of publicly available IPTV channels from all over the world
summary: IPTV is a collection of publicly available Internet Protocol television channels from around the world. The project provides structured M3U playlists that users can paste into any video player supporting live streaming to watch channels. Additionally, it offers access to an Electronic Program Guide (EPG), an underlying channel database, and an API. Intended for users seeking curated live television streams, the repository relies on user-submitted links to publicly available video stream URLs without hosting video files directly.

name: spec-kit
description: 💫 Toolkit to help you get started with SDD or any other process!
summary:
Spec Kit is an open-source toolkit designed to provide AI coding agents with structured processes, reusable templates, and documented outcomes for software development, bug fixing, and idea evaluation. 

The project supports three independent processes:
1. **Spec-Driven Development (SDD):** Guides users through defining requirements, building technical plans, generating tasks, implementing features, and converging code against specifications.
2. **Bug Fixing:** Separates diagnosis, repair, and verification into distinct steps (`assess`, `fix`, `test`) to scope and verify bug fixes against original symptoms.
3. **Idea Assessment:** Gathers evidence via intake, research, definition, shaping, and decision stages to evaluate ideas and produce evidence-backed go, clarify, or stop outcomes.

Intended for developers using AI coding agents, Spec Kit operates via a command-line interface (`specify-cli`) and slash commands executed in agent chat integrations like GitHub Copilot. 

Notable technologies and prerequisites used by the project include Python 3.11+, uv, and supported AI coding agents across Linux, macOS, and Windows. Customization is supported through extensions, presets, workflows, and bundles.

name: cc-switch
description: A cross-platform desktop All-in-One assistant for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Grok Build & Hermes Agent. Only official website: ccswitch.io
summary:
CC Switch is a cross-platform desktop manager designed to simplify configuration across multiple AI coding tools and agents, including Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Pi, and MiniMax Code. Built with Tauri 2, Rust, React, TypeScript, and SQLite, the application allows users to switch API providers with a single click and manage Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, prompts, and skills in a centralized location without manually editing JSON, TOML, YAML, or `.env` configuration files.

Main capabilities include over 90 provider presets (such as AWS Bedrock, NVIDIA NIM, and third-party relays), local API routing that automatically translates formats between Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini protocols, automatic failover queues, project-based state switching, session history browsing, usage tracking, and system tray quick-switching. The software targets developers and AI engineering teams looking to streamline multi-tool setups, manage subscription quotas, and reuse skills or MCP tools across different AI environments on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

name: PowerToys
description: Microsoft PowerToys is a collection of utilities that supercharge productivity and customization on Windows
summary:
Microsoft PowerToys is a collection of utilities designed for Windows power users to customize their operating system and streamline everyday tasks. Aimed at developers and power users, the project provides over 30 productivity tools—such as Advanced Paste, FancyZones, PowerToys Run, Text Extractor, Image Resizer, Keyboard Manager, and Mouse Without Borders—to optimize window management, workflow automation, system configuration, and file handling. 

The software utilizes technologies including WinUI 3, JavaScript, and TypeScript, and is actively developed with community contributions. Users can install PowerToys via standalone executable downloads from GitHub, the Microsoft Store, WinGet, Chocolatey, or Scoop.

name: go
description: The Go programming language
summary: Go is an open-source programming language designed to build simple, reliable, and efficient software. The project provides official binary distributions and instructions for installing from source for various operating systems and architectures. Distributed under a BSD-style license, Go relies on a community of contributors for its development, with resources for bug reports, proposals, and community questions.

name: free-for-dev
description: A list of SaaS, PaaS and IaaS offerings that have free tiers of interest to devops and infradev
summary:
The repository provides a curated, community-driven list of software-as-a-service (SaaS), platform-as-a-service (PaaS), infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS), and other developer-focused cloud offerings that feature free tiers. Its primary purpose is to help developers, system administrators, and DevOps practitioners discover free tools and services without spending time searching. 

The collection spans numerous categories, including major cloud providers (such as Google Cloud Platform, Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud, and Cloudflare), CI/CD pipelines, source code repositories, databases, monitoring, logging, security, authentication, API tools, storage, and hosting. Notable technologies and services featured across the list include Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis, and various AI/ML and serverless platforms. 

The intended users are infrastructure developers, open-source authors, and engineers seeking cost-effective or free cloud infrastructure and developer tooling. Contributions are maintained via pull requests, with strict criteria requiring services to offer an actual free tier rather than just a free trial, without hidden penalties like paid-only TLS restrictions.

name: fucking-algorithm
description: Crack LeetCode, not only how, but also why.
summary:
This repository provides a comprehensive collection of original tutorials and notes designed to help users master LeetCode algorithms and data structures through pattern-based thinking rather than simple code memorization. 

**Purpose and Capabilities**
The project aims to cultivate algorithmic problem-solving skills by breaking down approximately 500 LeetCode problems into repeatable frameworks and templates. It covers core topics such as dynamic programming, backtracking, breadth-first search (BFS), depth-first search (DFS), binary trees, greedy algorithms, sliding windows, two pointers, binary search, and graph theory. Additional sections address computer science fundamentals, design patterns, and mathematics. The repository also offers complementary tools including an algorithmic visualization panel, an AI teaching assistant, and browser/IDE extensions for Chrome, VS Code, and JetBrains to streamline the learning workflow directly on LeetCode.

**Intended Users**
The material targets self-taught programmers, software engineers preparing for job interviews, and beginners seeking clear, structured explanations to efficiently master coding interview problems.

**Notable Technologies**
Code examples and implementations are provided in multiple programming languages, primarily C++, Java, Golang, Python, and JavaScript.

name: ComfyUI
description: The most powerful and modular diffusion model GUI, api and backend with a graph/nodes interface. The fastest local inference engine in the world.
summary:
ComfyUI is a powerful, modular AI creation engine and inference engine featuring a visual node graph interface for building and running workflows spanning image, video, 3D model, audio, and text generation. It is designed for visual professionals and creatives seeking granular control over models, parameters, and outputs, with a strong focus on local consumer hardware optimization and low VRAM efficiency using asynchronous weight streaming. 

The software natively supports a wide range of open-source models—including Stable Diffusion (1.5, XL, 3.5), Flux.1, Flux.2, Wan 2.1, HunyuanVideo, CogVideoX, LTX-Video, Qwen series, Gemma, and various audio and 3D architectures—alongside closed-source model integrations via partner nodes. Intended users include creators, developers, and production pipelines requiring local execution, App Mode UI exposure, or API integration. Technologies utilized include Python, PyTorch (with CUDA, ROCm, XPU, and MPS support), and custom extensions managed through ComfyUI-Manager. ComfyUI is available cross-platform on Windows, Linux, and macOS via a desktop application, portable packages, command-line tooling, or cloud deployment.

name: gstack
description: Use Garry Tan's exact Claude Code setup: 23 opinionated tools that serve as CEO, Designer, Eng Manager, Release Manager, Doc Engineer, and QA
summary:
**gstack** is an open-source software factory that turns AI coding assistants—primarily Claude Code, along with OpenAI Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, and other agent harnesses—into a virtual engineering team. Conceived by Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, the project provides a structured process and a comprehensive suite of markdown-based slash commands covering the entire software development lifecycle: thinking, planning, building, reviewing, testing, shipping, and reflecting.

### Project Purpose
The project aims to empower single builders and technical founders to ship production-grade products at accelerated speeds by enforcing rigorous engineering workflows, catching production bugs, and automating routine development tasks through AI agents.

### Main Capabilities
* **Sprint & Review Pipeline:** Guides projects through specialized roles (CEO, Engineering Manager, Senior Designer, Developer Experience Lead, QA, Staff Engineer, and Chief Security Officer) via commands such as `/office-hours`, `/autoplan`, `/plan-eng-review`, `/review`, `/qa`, and `/ship`.
* **Design & Prototyping:** Includes visual exploration and production HTML generation tools (`/design-shotgun`, `/design-html`, `/design-consultation`) supporting vector diagrams, Mermaid/Excalidraw rendering, and PDF publishing (`/make-pdf`).
* **Browser Automation & QA:** Drives real logged-in sessions via the Aside browser or a bundled headless Chromium (`/browse`, `/qa`, `/open-gstack-browser`, `/scrape`) with local prompt-injection defense mechanisms and multi-agent coordination (`/pair-agent`).
* **Persistent Knowledge & State:** Integrates with GBrain (`/setup-gbrain`, `/sync-gbrain`) for cross-session agent memory and source indexing.
* **Safety & Guardrails:** Offers execution safety tools like `/careful`, `/freeze`, `/guard`, egress receipt auditing, and second-opinion code reviews (`/codex`, `/claude-code`).

### Intended Users
Technical founders, CEOs, engineering team leads, staff engineers, and AI coding assistant users looking for structured workflows rather than ad-hoc prompting.

### Notable Technologies
Built primarily with **TypeScript**, **Bun**, and **Node.js**, leveraging **Playwright** for browser automation, **Chromium**, and integrations with **Supabase**, **OpenAI Codex**, and **Claude Code**.

name: excalidraw
description: Virtual whiteboard for sketching hand-drawn like diagrams
summary:
Excalidraw is an open-source virtual whiteboard web application designed for creating hand-drawn style diagrams, wireframes, and sketches. Available as both an npm package for React integration and a hosted Progressive Web App (PWA), the project provides an infinite, customizable canvas with support for dark mode, shape libraries, image embedding, localization, and exports to formats such as PNG, SVG, and `.excalidraw` JSON files. 

Main capabilities include drawing tools (rectangles, circles, diamonds, arrows, lines, free-draw, and erasers), arrow-binding, labeled arrows, zoom and panning, undo and redo, real-time collaboration, and local-first autosaving. The hosted application additionally features end-to-end encryption and shareable read-only links. 

The software is intended for developers looking to embed drawing capabilities into custom applications via the `@excalidraw/excalidraw` package, as well as end-users seeking a collaborative whiteboarding tool. Technologies utilized include React, TypeScript, and modern web APIs supporting PWA functionality.

name: ui-ux-pro-max-skill
description: An AI skill that provides design intelligence for building professional UI/UX across multiple platforms.
summary:
UI UX Pro Max is an AI skill and design intelligence framework designed to help developers and AI coding agents build professional user interfaces and experiences across multiple platforms and frameworks. It provides structured guidance on UI/UX design through an intelligent reasoning engine that analyzes project requirements to generate complete, tailored design systems.

Key capabilities include:
- **Design System Generation:** An automated reasoning engine mapping project needs to industry rules, landing page patterns, UI styles, color palettes, and typography pairings.
- **Extensive Catalogs:** Searchable data sets featuring 79 UI styles, 192 industry-specific product types, 192 color palettes, 74 font pairings, 25 chart types, and 119 UX guidelines.
- **Stack-Specific Guidance:** Tailored guidelines supporting 22 technology stacks, including React, Next.js, Vue, Nuxt.js, Angular, Svelte, Astro, Laravel, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, Flutter, React Native, and various desktop platforms (such as JavaFX, WPF, and Avalonia).
- **CLI and Tool Integration:** Available via an npm CLI (`ui-ux-pro-max-cli`) providing commands for installation across numerous AI assistants (such as Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, and Gemini CLI), initialization, and persistent hierarchical design system generation.

Intended users include developers, UI/UX designers, and teams using AI coding assistants who need systematic, standards-compliant design logic and asset recommendations. Notable technologies utilized include Python 3.x for local search and generation scripts, Node.js/npm for the CLI package, and structured CSV/JSON databases.

name: hello-algo
description: 《Hello 算法》：动画图解、一键运行的数据结构与算法教程。支持简中、繁中、English、日本語，提供 Python, Java, C++, C, C#, JS, Go, Swift, Rust, Ruby, Kotlin, TS, Dart 等代码实现
summary: Hello-Algo is an open-source, beginner-friendly tutorial designed to teach data structures and algorithms through animated illustrations and runnable source code. The project aims to provide a smooth learning curve that helps learners explore fundamental algorithm mechanics and data structure implementations. Intended for algorithm beginners and programming students, the tutorial supports interactive learning, peer discussion, and multi-language translations. Notable technologies and programming languages featured in the code implementations include Python, Java, C++, C, C#, JavaScript, Go, Swift, Rust, Ruby, Kotlin, TypeScript, and Dart.

name: llama.cpp
description: LLM inference in C/C++
summary:
llama.cpp provides lightweight, high-performance Large Language Model (LLM) and Vision-Language Model (VLM) inference implemented in plain C/C++ with minimal setup. Built on top of the ggml library, the project is designed to run locally or in the cloud across a wide array of hardware.

Main capabilities include integer quantization ranging from 1.5-bit to 8-bit for reduced memory use and faster inference, a built-in web UI, an OpenAI-compatible API server (`llama serve`), a command-line interface (`llama cli`), and CPU+GPU hybrid inference. It supports diverse hardware backends such as Apple Silicon (via ARM NEON, Accelerate, and Metal), x86 architectures (via AVX, AVX2, AVX512, and AMX), RISC-V, NVIDIA GPUs (CUDA), AMD GPUs (HIP), Moore Threads GPUs (MUSA), Intel devices (OpenVINO, SYCL), Vulkan, and WebGPU. 

The project targets developers and users seeking efficient, low-dependency LLM and VLM execution across consumer hardware, mobile devices, and server environments.

name: 30-seconds-of-code
description: Coding articles to level up your development skills
summary: 30 seconds of code provides coding articles designed to help developers level up their skills. The project allows users to browse and search through articles and collections by name, tags, language, or description to view code snippets, explanations, and examples. Maintained by Angelos Chalaris, the repository invites users to report website problems or suggest improvements by opening issues, while new content contributions are not accepted. The website is built using Astro, hosted on Netlify, and integrated with GitHub, with imagery provided by Unsplash. Code snippets are licensed under the CC-BY-4.0 License.

name: MoneyPrinterTurbo
description: 利用 AI 大模型和自动化工作流，根据主题或关键词一键生成高清短视频。Generate HD short videos from a topic or keyword with an automated AI workflow.
summary:
MoneyPrinterTurbo is an all-in-one AI-powered short video generation tool designed to automatically create HD short videos from a given topic or keyword. It handles the complete pipeline—scriptwriting, voiceover generation, stock material matching, subtitle styling, and background music integration—yielding ready-to-publish vertical (9:16), horizontal (16:9), and square (1:1) video content for platforms like TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube Shorts. 

The application provides WebUI, API, CLI, and AI Agent interfaces supporting batch processing, task histories, and configuration exports. It integrates with major LLM, text-to-speech (TTS), and media generation providers including Kimi/Moonshot AI, OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, Azure, Volcengine Ark, MiniMax, ElevenLabs, Edge TTS, Fish Audio, and Kokoro, alongside local whisper-based transcription and stock footage platforms like Pexels, Pixabay, and Coverr.

Intended for content creators, developers, and AI-native teams looking to automate multimedia production, MoneyPrinterTurbo is built with Python 3.11+ and can be deployed cross-platform via Docker, pip/uv virtual environments, or pre-built Windows runtimes.

name: kubernetes
description: Production-Grade Container Scheduling and Management
