summary: Kubernetes (K8s) is an open-source system designed for managing containerized applications across multiple hosts, providing fundamental mechanisms for application deployment, maintenance, and scaling. Built upon Google’s experience running production workloads at scale using Borg and community practices, the project is hosted by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF). Kubernetes is intended for organizations and developers seeking to run container-packaged, dynamically scheduled, and microservices-oriented architectures. The codebase is developed using Go and Docker environments, and the project supports building from source and contributing via its community repositories.

name: codex
description: Lightweight coding agent that runs in your terminal
summary:
Codex CLI is a local coding agent developed by OpenAI that runs directly on a user's computer. Its primary purpose is to assist developers with coding tasks through a command-line interface, with integrations also available for code editors like VS Code, Cursor, and Windsurf, alongside desktop and cloud-based options. 

Intended for developers and users with ChatGPT plans (including Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, and Enterprise) or API keys, Codex CLI can authenticate via ChatGPT sign-in. Installation is supported on macOS, Linux, and Windows via shell scripts, npm (`@openai/codex`), Homebrew (`brew install --cask codex`), or pre-compiled binaries obtained through GitHub Releases.

name: react-native
description: A framework for building native applications using React
summary: React Native enables developers to create native applications for Android, iOS, and other platforms using React and JavaScript. Its core capabilities include rendering UI primitives with native code to ensure platform-standard gestures, text scaling, and accessibility. It supports declarative UI, components, hooks, Suspense, and Fast Refresh for developer velocity without rebuilding the native app. Developers can extend capabilities using Native Modules to call platform code directly or leverage existing libraries. Frameworks such as Expo provide production-ready toolboxes with file-based routing and native modules, though projects can also be built without a framework. The project is intended for developers building mobile and multi-platform applications. Notable technologies mentioned include React, JavaScript, Android, iOS, and Expo.

name: rustdesk
description: An open-source remote desktop application designed for self-hosting, as an alternative to TeamViewer.
summary:
RustDesk is an open-source, full-control remote desktop software written in Rust. It works out of the box with zero configuration required, allowing users to maintain complete ownership of their data and security by utilizing built-in rendezvous and relay servers or hosting custom servers. 

Key capabilities include remote desktop viewing and control, cross-platform file transfers, audio streaming, clipboard synchronization, and TCP tunneling. The project supports desktop and mobile environments using the Flutter framework (alongside legacy Sciter UI support). 

The codebase utilizes notable technologies and libraries such as Cargo, vcpkg, libvpx, libyuv, opus, and aom. It is structured into modular components including `libs/scrap` for screen capture, `libs/enigo` for cross-platform mouse and keyboard simulation, `libs/hbb_common` for video codecs and networking utilities, and `flutter` for the primary graphical user interface. The software targets general users and administrators looking for a self-hosted alternative to traditional remote desktop solutions.

name: ui
description: Composable, accessible components with thoughtful defaults. Build your own component library with code you can customize, extend, and make your own.
summary: shadcn/ui provides a set of beautifully designed, customizable, and extendable components intended to help developers build their own component libraries. Operating under an open-source and open-code model, the project is designed for developers seeking flexible UI elements that they can adapt, extend, and make their own.

name: graphify
description: Turn any codebase, with its docs, SQL schemas, configs, and PDFs, into a queryable knowledge graph. A /graphify skill for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini CLI: local deterministic AST parsing, every edge explained, no vector store.
summary:
Graphify is a developer tool and AI coding assistant extension designed to parse and map entire codebases, documentation, PDFs, images, and videos into a queryable knowledge graph instead of relying on file grepping or vector embeddings. 

Main capabilities include local AST parsing across over 37 programming languages via tree-sitter, cross-file link resolution, confidence-tagged relationship edges (`EXTRACTED` vs `INFERRED`), Leiden community detection, god-node identification, design rationale extraction, path tracing, and plain-language querying (`graphify query`, `graphify path`, `graphify explain`). It supports integration with over 20 AI platforms—including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Aider, and GitHub Copilot CLI—and offers an MCP server interface, headless CI extraction, and outputs like HTML visualizations, Markdown reports, wikis, and graph exports (Neo4j, FalkorDB, GraphML). 

Intended users are software developers and development teams seeking structured, local-first code intelligence and context retrieval. Notable technologies utilized include tree-sitter, Python, SQLite, Markdown, MCP (Model Context Protocol), and various LLM backends (such as Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Ollama, and AWS Bedrock).

name: electron
description: :electron: Build cross-platform desktop apps with JavaScript, HTML, and CSS
summary: Electron is a cross-platform desktop application framework that enables developers to build native desktop apps using JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. Based on Node.js and Chromium, Electron provides prebuilt binaries supporting macOS, Windows, and Linux operating systems across Intel, Apple Silicon, and ARM architectures. It is intended for software developers building desktop applications and is utilized by prominent projects like Visual Studio Code. Notable technologies and tools associated with the project include Node.js, Chromium, npm, and Electron Fiddle for experimenting with APIs and packaging code examples.

name: node
description: Node.js JavaScript runtime ✨🐢🚀✨
summary: Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime environment supported by the OpenJS Foundation. It provides infrastructure for building, downloading, verifying, and releasing software using JavaScript, following semantic versioning across Current, LTS, and nightly release channels. The project is intended for software developers and contributors building applications or contributing to the core runtime, operating under an open governance model guided by a Technical Steering Committee and managed via collaborative workflows. Node.js is licensed under the MIT License.

name: Awesome-Hacking
description: A collection of various awesome lists for hackers, pentesters and security researchers
summary:
Awesome Hacking is a curated collection of awesome lists, tools, frameworks, and resources tailored for hackers, penetration testers, security researchers, and bug bounty hunters. The project compiles a vast range of specialized topics across cybersecurity domains, including Android and iOS security, application security, asset discovery, bug bounty programs, cellular hacking (3G/4G/5G), CI/CD attacks, CTF frameworks, detection engineering, DevSecOps, drone hacking, embedded and IoT security, fuzzing, honeypots, incident response, industrial control system (ICS) security, malware analysis, OSINT, password cracking, penetration testing, prompt injection, red teaming, reverse engineering, threat intelligence, vehicle security, and web3 security. 

Intended for security professionals, ethical hackers, developers, and learners seeking educational materials or training environments, the repository serves as a centralized index linking to diverse open-source tools, write-ups, wordlists, and reference guides. It encompasses specialized technologies and platforms such as Node.js, PHP, YARA rules, Suricata, Docker-Compose, and Tor, alongside various security testing and analysis methodologies.

name: generative-ai-for-beginners
description: 21 Lessons, Get Started Building with Generative AI
summary:
This repository contains a comprehensive 21-lesson curriculum designed to teach beginners how to build Generative AI applications. Created by Microsoft Cloud Advocates, the project's purpose is to cover foundational concepts and practical implementations related to Large Language Models (LLMs), Small Language Models (SLMs), and artificial intelligence application development. 

Main capabilities and curriculum topics include prompt engineering, text generation, chat applications, vector databases, image generation, low-code AI development, function calling, user experience design, AI security, LLMOps, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), AI agents, fine-tuning, and working with specific model families such as Mistral and Meta. 

Intended users are developers, students, and beginners looking to acquire hands-on artificial intelligence skills. The course provides code samples in Python and TypeScript, along with multi-language translations and resources supporting technologies such as Azure OpenAI Service, OpenAI API, Microsoft Foundry Models, Foundry Local, and Hugging Face.

name: rust
description: Empowering everyone to build reliable and efficient software.
summary:
This is the main source code repository for the Rust programming language, containing the compiler, standard library, and documentation. Rust is designed to empower everyone to build reliable and efficient software. 

Key capabilities and features include high performance and memory efficiency suitable for critical services and embedded devices, along with a rich type system and ownership model that guarantee memory and thread safety at compile-time to ensure reliability. Productivity is supported via advanced tooling such as the package manager and build tool Cargo, the auto-formatter rustfmt, the linter Clippy, and editor support through rust-analyzer, alongside comprehensive documentation and clear compiler diagnostics. 

The project is intended for developers building reliable and efficient software. It is distributed primarily under the MIT license and the Apache License (Version 2.0).

name: awesome-design-md
description: A collection of DESIGN.md files analysis by popular brand design systems. Drop one into your project and let coding agents generate a matching UI.
summary:
This repository is a curated collection of DESIGN.md files extracted from real-world websites, AI platforms, developer tools, SaaS applications, and retro web archives. Designed for AI coding agents and tools like Google Stitch, the project provides plain-text design system documents that define color palettes, typography rules, component stylings, layout principles, and elevation systems to help AI agents generate visually consistent user interfaces. 

The collection includes ready-to-use DESIGN.md files paired with preview HTML catalogs for major platforms such as Claude, Vercel, Supabase, Linear, Stripe, Apple, and historical sites like Dell (1996) and Nintendo (2001). Intended users include developers, designers, and AI builders seeking to enforce strict design depth and token consistency during AI-assisted UI generation. Technologies and concepts utilized include Markdown, Google Stitch DESIGN.md specifications, design tokens, and web development frameworks.

name: free-programming-books-zh_CN
description: :books: 免费的计算机编程类中文书籍，欢迎投稿
summary:
This repository is a curated index of free programming books and resources available in Chinese. It serves as a comprehensive directory for developers, students, and technology enthusiasts seeking learning materials, tutorials, and documentation across a wide range of computer science topics. 

The collection covers language-agnostic subjects such as operating systems, artificial intelligence, distributed systems, algorithms, design patterns, databases (including MySQL, PostgreSQL, and NoSQL), web development, networking, version control tools, and editors. It also provides extensive resources for specific programming languages and technologies, including C/C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, Go, Rust, Ruby, PHP, Swift, Kotlin, and mobile development frameworks like Android and iOS. 

Intended for programmers at all levels—from beginners learning foundational concepts to advanced engineers exploring specialized fields like large language models (LLMs) and system architecture—the repository aggregates community-contributed links, official documentation translations, and open-source guides. No specific proprietary technologies or deployment frameworks are required to access the content, as it functions purely as an informational index and reading list.

name: godot
description: Godot Engine – Multi-platform 2D and 3D game engine
summary:
Godot Engine is a feature-packed, cross-platform game engine designed to create 2D and 3D games from a unified interface. It provides a comprehensive set of common tools that allow users to focus on game development. Games created with the engine can be exported with one click to multiple platforms, including major desktop platforms (Linux, macOS, Windows), mobile platforms (Android, iOS), web-based platforms, and consoles. 

The project is free, open source, and licensed under the MIT license, with development supported by the Godot Foundation. Intended users include game developers, designers, and programmers seeking an independent, community-driven engine. Notable technologies and platform capabilities mentioned include support for 2D and 3D rendering, cross-platform export templates, and a built-in class reference accessible directly from the Godot editor.

name: v2rayN
description: A GUI client for Windows, Linux and macOS, support Xray and sing-box and others
summary: v2rayN is a graphical user interface (GUI) desktop client designed for Windows, Linux, and macOS. Its primary purpose is to manage and run proxy configurations by supporting backend routing cores such as Xray-core and sing-box, among others. The software targets desktop users seeking to configure and utilize network proxy and tunneling services across multiple hardware architectures, including x64, x86, arm64, riscv64, and loong64.

name: browser-use
description: Agents that use the browser.
summary:
Browser Use is an open-source AI browser agent designed to navigate the web like a human, executing tasks such as booking appointments, filling forms, and solving CAPTCHAs. 

Main capabilities include controlling local or remote web browsers (via CDP), executing browser actions, registering custom tools, and integrating with external systems like the Anthropic SDK. Users can operate Browser Use through three primary paths: a fully hosted cloud platform with managed infrastructure and stealth capabilities, a command-line interface (CLI) to connect existing agents (such as Claude Code or Codex) to a browser, or a Python and TypeScript library for local development. 

The project is intended for developers and users seeking to automate browser workflows, build AI-driven web scrapers, or integrate browser capabilities into autonomous agents. Notable technologies utilized include Python, TypeScript, uv, OpenAI, Anthropic SDK, and CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol).

name: three.js
description: JavaScript 3D Library.
summary: Three.js is an easy-to-use, lightweight, cross-browser, general-purpose JavaScript 3D library designed to create and display animated 3D graphics in web browsers. Its current core builds include WebGL and WebGPU renderers, with SVG and CSS3D renderers available as addons. The library enables users to set up scenes, cameras, geometric shapes, materials, and meshes, and render them directly to the DOM via a viewport.

name: immich
description: High performance self-hosted photo and video management solution.
summary: Immich is a high-performance, self-hosted photo and video management solution. It provides capabilities for uploading, viewing, backing up, and organizing media assets across both mobile and web platforms. Main features include automated and background backups, multi-user support, duplicate prevention, RAW format support, EXIF and map metadata viewing, global map displays, folder views, archives, favorites, and stacked photos. Additionally, Immich supports advanced discovery capabilities such as facial recognition and clustering, search via metadata, objects, faces, and CLIP, as well as memory flashbacks (e.g., photos from years past). Collaboration and sharing features comprise shared albums, partner sharing, and public sharing. Administrative and integration capabilities include user management, OAuth support, API keys, user-defined storage structures, and offline support on mobile devices.

name: awesome-mac
description:  This project is dedicated to collecting high-quality macOS software and organizing them systematically by different categories for easy search and use.
summary:
Awesome Mac is a curated, open-source collection of high-quality macOS software, applications, developer tools, and utilities systematically organized by category. Its primary purpose is to help macOS users easily discover, search, and evaluate authentic applications ranging from reading and writing tools, IDEs, terminal apps, AI tools, design suites, and cloud storage to system utilities, window managers, and security solutions. 

The repository categorizes items using clear indicators for open-source software (OSS), freeware, App Store availability, native applications, and related awesome lists. Intended for Mac users, developers, designers, and power users looking for reliable software recommendations, the collection spans diverse technologies and frameworks, including native Swift and AppKit applications, terminal utilities, command-line interfaces, and cross-platform runtimes. Contributions are welcomed through pull requests following established guidelines, with localized editions available in Chinese, Korean, and Japanese.

name: d3
description: Bring data to life with SVG, Canvas and HTML. :bar_chart::chart_with_upwards_trend::tada:
summary: D3 (D3.js) is a free, open-source JavaScript library designed for visualizing data. Utilizing a low-level approach built on web standards, D3 provides flexibility for authoring dynamic, data-driven graphics. It serves as a foundational building block for higher-level chart libraries and is intended for data practitioners and developers seeking to create customized data visualizations.

name: pi
description: AI agent toolkit: unified LLM API, agent loop, TUI, coding agent CLI
summary:
Pi is a minimal, extensible agent harness and interactive coding agent CLI designed to be adapted to custom workflows. Users can customize it using extensions, skills, prompt templates, and themes, which can be bundled as Pi packages and shared via npm or git. 

The project's main capabilities include running interactively, automation via print or JSON modes, remote control over RPC, and building applications using the Pi TypeScript SDK. 

Notable technologies and packages included in the monorepo:
- **@earendil-works/chord**: Standalone application-composition runtime.
- **@earendil-works/pi-telemetry**: Vendor-neutral telemetry contracts and reference adapters.
- **@earendil-works/pi-ai**: Unified multi-provider LLM API supporting OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and others.
- **@earendil-works/pi-durable**: Durable conversation, task, and document runtime.
- **@earendil-works/pi-agent-core**: Agent runtime featuring tool calling and state management.
- **@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent**: Interactive coding agent CLI.
- **@earendil-works/pi-tui**: Terminal UI library utilizing differential rendering.
- **TypeScript & Node.js** (requires Node.js 22.19 or newer).

Pi is intended for developers seeking a customizable, extensible AI agent harness and interactive coding agent environment with multi-provider LLM integration.

name: tauri
description: Build smaller, faster, and more secure desktop and mobile applications with a web frontend.
summary:
Tauri is a framework designed for developers to build tiny, fast binaries for major operating systems including Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and iOS. The project purpose is to enable the creation of cross-platform applications using any front-end framework that compiles to HTML, JS, and CSS, paired with a Rust-sourced backend binary that exposes an interactive API. 

Main capabilities include a built-in app bundler supporting formats such as `.app`, `.dmg`, `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.AppImage`, `.exe`, and `.msi`, a built-in self updater for desktop platforms, system tray icons, native notifications, and a native WebView Protocol that avoids running a localhost HTTP(S) server. 

Notable technologies and libraries utilized include Rust, HTML, JavaScript, CSS, `tao` for window handling, and `WRY` to interface with system webviews (WKWebView, WebView2, WebKitGTK, and Android System WebView). The framework also provides a VS Code extension and a GitHub Action for CI integration. Tauri is intended for developers seeking to build efficient desktop and mobile applications.

name: TypeScript
description: TypeScript is a superset of JavaScript that compiles to clean JavaScript output.
summary: TypeScript is a programming language developed by Microsoft for application-scale JavaScript development. It adds optional types to JavaScript, supporting tooling for large-scale applications that run on any browser, host, or operating system. TypeScript compiles down to readable, standards-based JavaScript. The project is intended for JavaScript developers seeking enhanced tooling and type safety.

name: supabase
description: The Postgres development platform. Supabase gives you a dedicated Postgres database to build your web, mobile, and AI applications.
summary:
Supabase is an open-source Postgres development platform designed to provide a Firebase-like developer experience using enterprise-grade open-source tools. Its main capabilities include a hosted Postgres database, authentication and authorization, auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs, realtime subscriptions, database and edge functions, file storage, an AI and vector embeddings toolkit, and a management dashboard. 

Intended users are developers seeking an open-source alternative to backend-as-a-service providers for building web and mobile applications. Notable technologies utilized in the architecture include PostgreSQL, Elixir, Realtime, PostgREST, GoTrue, S3-compatible storage, pg_graphql, postgres-meta, and Envoy.

name: papers-we-love
description: Papers from the computer science community to read and discuss.
summary:
Papers We Love (PWL) is a community-driven repository and directory designed for reading, discussing, and learning about academic computer science papers. It serves as a centralized collection point for documents and links scattered across the web, occasionally hosting papers directly while respecting content licenses. 

The project is intended for computer science enthusiasts, researchers, and developers who want to explore academic literature, participate in local chapter meetups, and engage in discussions. The repository provides a curated directory structure, auxiliary reading resources on how to analyze academic articles, and a download script (`./scripts/download.sh`) that scrapes markdown files to fetch linked PDF papers. Community interaction is supported via a Discord server and a YouTube channel featuring past presentations.

name: whisper
description: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
summary:
**Project Purpose:**
Whisper is a general-purpose, multitasking speech recognition system designed to process audio through a unified model, replacing traditional multi-stage speech-processing pipelines.

**Main Capabilities:**
The project performs multilingual speech recognition, speech translation, spoken language identification, and voice activity detection. It is available in multiple model sizes (ranging from tiny to large and turbo) to offer speed and accuracy tradeoffs across different hardware configurations and tasks.

**Intended Users:**
Developers and researchers needing automatic speech recognition (ASR), translation, or audio transcription capabilities via command-line tools or Python APIs.

**Notable Technologies:**
- PyTorch
- Transformer sequence-to-sequence architecture
- OpenAI's tiktoken (tokenizer)
- ffmpeg (command-line tool)
- Python (compatible with versions 3.8 to 3.11)

name: frp
description: A fast reverse proxy to help you expose a local server behind a NAT or firewall to the internet.
summary:
frp is a fast reverse proxy designed to expose local servers located behind NATs or firewalls to the Internet. It supports TCP, UDP, HTTP, and HTTPS protocols, as well as a P2P connection mode, enabling requests to be forwarded to internal services via domain names. The project aims to provide comprehensive intranet penetration and tunneling capabilities, including features such as TCP/HTTP port multiplexing, load balancing, health checks, bandwidth limits, encryption and compression via TLS, token and OIDC authentication, client plugins, an SSH tunnel gateway, and an alpha VirtualNet feature for IP-level routing over a TUN interface. 

Intended for developers and administrators needing secure external access to internal network resources, frp consists of a server component (`frps`) deployed on a public IP address and a client component (`frpc`) run on the local machine. The project is implemented in Go and supports TOML, YAML, and JSON configuration formats.

name: TradingAgents
description: TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework
summary:
TradingAgents is a multi-agent LLM financial trading framework designed for research purposes to simulate the dynamics of real-world trading firms. The project utilizes specialized, LLM-powered agents—including fundamental, sentiment, news, and technical analysts, as well as bullish and bearish researchers, a trader, a risk management team, and a portfolio manager—that collaborate through structured discussions to evaluate market conditions and formulate trading decisions.

Intended users include researchers and developers exploring multi-agent financial analysis. The framework supports diverse market instruments, including global stocks across various international exchanges, crypto, and macroeconomic indicators. 

Key capabilities encompass parallel analysts, point-in-time data integrity with SEC EDGAR fundamentals, sentiment screening of social posts via TypeSafe's Jev, persistent memory logs with reflection, LangGraph-based checkpoint resume, portfolio-aware runs, and a grid-based backtesting engine. The architecture features extensive multi-provider LLM support—including OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, xAI Grok, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, MiniMax, OpenRouter, Mistral, Kimi, Groq, NVIDIA NIM, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints—as well as a command-line interface (CLI) and Docker support.

name: caveman
description: 🪨 why use many token when few token do trick. Viral skill + proxy for coding agents that cuts 65% of tokens by talking like a caveman.
summary:
Caveman is an open-source tool designed to reduce token consumption for AI coding agents by minimizing conversational prose and compressing context payloads. 

The project offers three main capabilities:
1. **The Skill**: A set of rule files and prompts that cause agents (such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, and Copilot) to communicate with concise, direct language.
2. **The Proxy**: A local CLI-driven proxy that intercepts requests and compresses bulky tool outputs like logs, JSON, diffs, search results, and test outputs before sending them to the AI provider. Originals are stored locally in a SQLite database with recovery handles, enabling agents to retrieve full context when needed.
3. **The Middleware**: Software wrappers for TypeScript and Python frameworks (including Vercel AI SDK, LangChain, OpenAI, and Anthropic) that apply the same input compression and retrieval tools directly inside custom applications.

Caveman is intended for developers and engineers utilizing LLM-based coding assistants and agents who want to lower API billing costs without sacrificing code quality or correctness. Notable technologies and components include TypeScript, Python, SQLite, an MCP (Model Context Protocol) toolkit, browser/ARIA tree compression, pixel-mode rendering for skill optimization, and support for over 30 agent ecosystems.

name: axios
description: Promise based HTTP client for the browser and node.js
summary:
Axios is a promise-based HTTP client designed for both the browser and Node.js environments. Its core purpose is to simplify making asynchronous HTTP requests, handling data transformation, managing request and response interceptors, and supporting request cancellation via built-in APIs like `AbortController`. 

Main capabilities include making `XMLHttpRequests` in browsers, executing `http` requests in Node.js, automatic serialization and parsing of JSON, form-urlencoded, and `multipart/form-data` formats, progress capturing for uploads and downloads, rate limiting, and client-side protection against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF). It also features an extensible fetch adapter and experimental HTTP/2 support.

Intended users are web and backend JavaScript developers building applications that require robust network communication, API integration, and type-safe request handling. 

Notable technologies and terms associated with the project include TypeScript, Node.js, browser environments, ECMAScript Promises, `AxiosHeaders`, `URLSearchParams`, and `FormData`.

name: deno
description: A modern runtime for JavaScript and TypeScript.
summary: Deno is a JavaScript, TypeScript, and WebAssembly runtime designed with secure defaults and a focus on developer experience. It is commonly used to build web servers, command-line tools, and other applications. The project is built using V8, Rust, and Tokio, and it integrates with the Deno Standard Library and JSR, an open-source package registry for modern JavaScript and TypeScript.

name: gemini-cli
description: An open-source AI agent that brings the power of Gemini directly into your terminal.
summary:
Gemini CLI is an open-source AI agent designed for developers to bring the capabilities of Gemini directly into the terminal. Intended for developers working in the command line, it facilitates code understanding, generation, debugging, and task automation. 

Main capabilities include interactive querying and editing of large codebases, natural language troubleshooting, multimodal application generation, conversation checkpointing, and non-interactive script execution. It features built-in tools for Google Search grounding, file system operations, shell commands, and web fetching, alongside Model Context Protocol (MCP) support for custom integrations and extensions. 

The project supports authentication via Google accounts, Gemini API keys, and Vertex AI. Notable technologies and protocols utilized include the Gemini model family, MCP, and standard packaging formats via npm, Homebrew, MacPorts, and Anaconda.

name: LLMs-from-scratch
description: Implement a ChatGPT-like LLM in PyTorch from scratch, step by step
summary:
This repository is the official code companion for the book *Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch)* by Sebastian Raschka. It provides step-by-step instructions and code for developing, pretraining, and finetuning a GPT-like large language model from the ground up. 

Main capabilities include working with text data, implementing attention mechanisms (such as multi-head attention), building a GPT model, pretraining on unlabeled data, and finetuning for text classification and instruction following. Additional topics covered in bonus materials include byte pair encoding (BPE) tokenizers, parameter-efficient finetuning with LoRA, direct preference optimization (DPO), and alternative architectures like Llama, Qwen, Gemma, and Olmo.

Intended users include students, researchers, and developers with a strong foundation in Python and familiarity with deep neural networks who want to understand how LLMs work internally. 

The project is implemented using Python and **PyTorch**, utilizing standard libraries and conventional hardware without requiring external LLM frameworks.

name: nodebestpractices
description: ✅ The Node.js best practices list (July 2026)
summary:
This repository serves as a comprehensive, community-curated collection of Node.js best practices, architectural tips, and style guides. Its primary purpose is to provide developers, engineers, and consultants with actionable guidelines for building, testing, securing, and deploying robust Node.js applications. 

The project covers several core areas:
- **Project Architecture:** Structuring solutions by business components, layering with 3-tier patterns, and managing configurations.
- **Error Handling:** Distinguishing operational from programmer errors, centralized error management, and utilizing async/await properly.
- **Code Style:** Applying patterns such as strict equality, explicit module entry points, and leveraging ESLint and Prettier.
- **Testing & Quality:** Writing API and component tests using the AAA pattern, checking coverage, and mocking external services.
- **Production & Docker:** Ensuring statelessness, optimizing CPU core utilization, setting memory limits, using multi-stage Docker builds, and monitoring applications via APM products.
- **Security:** Implementing OWASP top 10 recommendations, securing HTTP headers, preventing injection vulnerabilities, hashing passwords with bcrypt/scrypt, and scanning dependencies.

Intended users include backend developers, DevOps engineers, and full-stack teams seeking production-grade standards. Notable technologies and tools referenced throughout the repository include Node.js, TypeScript, Docker, Kubernetes, Express, Fastify, Nest.js, ESLint, Pino, Winston, Jest, Mocha, and SonarQube.

name: weekly
description: 科技爱好者周刊，每周五发布
summary: 科技爱好者周刊是一个每周五发布、旨在记录并分享值得关注的科技内容与资源的开源项目。该周刊内容涵盖人工智能、软件开发、开源生态、职业发展、互联网趋势及科技行业观察等多方面的主题，并通过社区贡献机制接收文章、软件及资源的投稿。此外，项目还设有“谁在招人”讨论区，为程序员和求职者提供免费的就业信息与岗位发布服务。该仓库主要面向广大科技爱好者、程序员以及寻求职业发展机会的求职者。

name: terminal
description: The new Windows Terminal and the original Windows console host, all in the same place!
summary:
Windows Terminal is a modern, feature-rich command-line application for Windows users, supporting tabs, rich text, themes, and configurability. The repository also contains the Windows console host (`conhost.exe`), shared components such as a DirectWrite-based text layout and rendering engine, a text buffer supporting UTF-16 and UTF-8, and a VT parser/emitter. 

Intended for command-line users and developers on Windows 10 (build 19041+) and Windows 11, the project enables efficient interaction with command-line infrastructure through tools like ConPTY. Notable technologies used include C++, Visual Studio, WinUI, the Windows Implementation Libraries (WIL), and Standard Template Library (STL) containers.

name: DeepSeek-V3
summary:
DeepSeek-V3 is a 671B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model featuring 37B activated parameters per token, developed by DeepSeek-AI. Designed for efficient inference and training, it incorporates Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA), DeepSeekMoE architecture, an auxiliary-loss-free load balancing strategy, and a multi-token prediction (MTP) training objective. The repository provides weights, evaluations, and deployment guides for local and cloud usage.

Intended users include developers, researchers, and enterprises seeking high-performance open-source or commercially usable language models for tasks like code generation, mathematics, reasoning, and multi-turn chat. 

The project supports notable technologies such as FP8 mixed-precision training, PyTorch, Triton, Transformers, safetensors, SGLang, LMDeploy, TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, LightLLM, and MindIE for Huawei Ascend NPUs, with compatibility across NVIDIA and AMD GPUs.

name: pytorch
description: Tensors and Dynamic neural networks in Python with strong GPU acceleration
summary:
PyTorch is a Python package that provides tensor computations with strong GPU acceleration and deep neural networks built on a tape-based autograd system. Designed for deep learning researchers and developers, PyTorch functions as a NumPy replacement for GPU-accelerated operations and as a dynamic, flexible deep learning research platform. Its core components include `torch`, `torch.autograd`, `torch.jit` (TorchScript), `torch.nn`, `torch.multiprocessing`, and `torch.utils`. 

Notable technologies and libraries integrated or utilized within PyTorch include Python, NumPy, SciPy, Cython, Numba, Intel MKL, Intel oneDNN, NVIDIA CUDA, cuDNN, NCCL, Magma, and AMD ROCm. The framework emphasizes a Python-first approach, imperative execution experiences, lean memory management, and straightforward C/C++ or Python extension capabilities.

name: create-react-app
description: Set up a modern web app by running one command.
summary:
Create React App is a deprecated command-line tool designed to set up and bootstrap single-page React applications with no initial build configuration. It provides a single curated dependency that preconfigures build tools including webpack, Babel, ESLint, and a unit test runner, allowing developers to focus entirely on writing code. 

The project supports macOS, Windows, and Linux operating systems, and requires Node 14.0.0 or later. It includes built-in commands for running a live development server with hot reloading, executing interactive unit tests, and generating minified production bundles containing JavaScript, CSS, and static assets. It also offers syntax support for React, JSX, ES6, TypeScript, Flow, and language extras like the object spread operator, alongside autoprefixed CSS, offline-first service workers, and web app manifests. 

Intended users include developers learning React, individuals starting new single-page React applications, and creators building component examples. Notable technologies integrated into the ecosystem include webpack, Babel, ESLint, React, JSX, TypeScript, and Yarn.

name: fastapi
description: FastAPI framework, high performance, easy to learn, fast to code, ready for production
summary:
FastAPI is a modern, high-performance web framework designed for building APIs with Python based on standard Python type hints. Its primary purpose is to enable fast API development with fewer bugs, intuitive editor autocompletion, high scalability, and production-ready code. 

Main capabilities include automatic data validation, input and output data serialization, dependency injection, WebSockets integration, security and authentication support (including OAuth2 and HTTP Basic), and automatic interactive API documentation generated via Swagger UI and ReDoc. 

Intended users are Python developers ranging from individual creators to enterprise teams building web services, REST APIs, and machine learning endpoints. 

Notable technologies and dependencies used include Starlette for web handling, Pydantic for data validation, Uvicorn as the ASGI server, and open standards such as OpenAPI and JSON Schema. The project is licensed under the MIT license.

name: neovim
description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability
summary: Neovim is a project that aggressively refactors Vim to simplify maintenance, encourage contributions, enable advanced UIs without core modifications, and maximize extensibility. Its main capabilities include support for modern GUIs, API access from languages such as C/C++, C#, Go, JavaScript/Node.js, Lua, Python, and Rust, an embedded scriptable terminal emulator, asynchronous job control, shared data (shada) across multiple editor instances, XDG base directories support, and compatibility with most existing Vim plugins (including Ruby and Python plugins). Intended users include developers and text-editor users seeking a modernized, extensible, and scriptable alternative to Vim. The project uses CMake for building and relies on technologies including Lua, Vimscript, and Msgpack-RPC.

name: HowToCook
description: Programmer's guide about how to cook at home.
summary:
程序员做饭指南（HowToCook）是一个由社区驱动和维护的开源项目，旨在用清晰、精准、形式化的描述整理常见菜谱，为习惯了形式语言的程序员在家做饭提供便利。项目收录了涵盖素菜、荤菜、水产、早餐、主食、半成品加工、汤与粥、饮料、酱料、甜品等全方位的菜谱，并提供厨房准备、洗碗指南、去腥、食品安全及高压锅、空气炸锅、微波炉等厨具使用技巧，以及焯水、炒、煎、蒸、煮、高级专业术语和油温判断等进阶烹饪知识。

该项目主要通过网页端（howtocook.aiursoft.com）进行可视化浏览，并支持通过 Docker 容器（`aiursoft/howtocookviewer`）进行本地部署。社区成员可以通过提交 Pull Request 贡献新菜谱或修改现有内容。项目相关技术栈与工具主要涉及 Docker。

name: angular
description: Deliver web apps with confidence 🚀
summary:
Angular is a development platform for building mobile and desktop web applications using TypeScript, JavaScript, and other languages. Designed for web developers, the platform provides robust tooling, including the Angular Command Line Interface (CLI) and Angular Material, to build scalable, cross-platform applications. 

Main capabilities include component-based architecture, templates, forms, server-side rendering (SSR), Angular Elements, schematics, lazy loading, and animations. The ecosystem supports modern web development workflows from local workspace setup using Node.js and npm to project generation and production deployment.

name: agent-skills
description: Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.
summary:
Agent Skills is a production-grade collection of workflows, quality gates, and best practices designed to consistently guide AI coding agents through every phase of the software development lifecycle. The project provides 25 structured, portable skills—mapped to lifecycle commands like `/spec`, `/plan`, `/build`, `/test`, `/review`, and `/ship`—alongside 4 specialist agent personas and 7 reference checklists. 

Targeting developers, engineering teams, and AI coding agents across more than 70 tools (such as Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Codex, and Windsurf), it enforces disciplined development practices such as test-driven development, contract-first API design, OWASP-based security hardening, and Core Web Vitals performance optimization. The repository incorporates engineering principles from Google's engineering culture, including Hyrum's Law, trunk-based development, and Chesterton's Fence. Technologies and tools referenced include Chrome DevTools MCP, OpenTelemetry, Markdown, TOML, Git, and various CLI interfaces.

name: every-programmer-should-know
description: A collection of (mostly) technical things every software developer should know about
summary: This repository is a curated collection of technical resources, books, courses, articles, and tools intended for software developers regardless of their skill level or tech stack. The project serves as a comprehensive knowledge base covering core computer science topics, algorithms, data structures, numbers, strings, latency, time, memory, distributed systems, machine learning, regular expressions, security, user experience, search engine optimization, software architecture, code design, engineering philosophy, development practices, career guidance, resume building, open source, remote work, problem-solving, soft skills, mental health, academic papers, free books, development services, software licenses, coding practice platforms, educational games, and platform engineering. The intended users are software programmers, developers, engineers, and technical founders looking to improve their technical expertise, career prospects, and daily workflows.

name: ant-design
description: An enterprise-class UI design language and React UI library
summary:
Ant Design is an enterprise-class UI design language and React UI library tailored for web applications. It provides a comprehensive set of high-quality React components out of the box, supporting modern browsers, Server-side Rendering, and Electron. 

The project is built with TypeScript to ensure predictable static types and includes a full package of design resources and development tools. Key capabilities include internationalization support for dozens of languages and powerful theme customization powered by CSS-in-JS. It is primarily intended for developers building enterprise web applications, dashboards, and desktop applications using React.

name: open-design
description: 🎨 Best DeepSeek Harness Design Plugin. The open-source Claude Design alternative. 🖥️ Local-first desktop app. 🖼️ Your coding agent becomes the design engine: prototypes, landing pages, dashboards, slides, images & video — real files, HTML/PDF/PPTX/MP4 export. 🤖 Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / DeepSeek Harness / OpenCode & 20+ CLIs via BYOK.
summary:
OpenDesign is a collaborative, open-source design agent workspace licensed under Apache 2.0. Serving as an alternative to proprietary tools like Claude Design, the project enables teams to build, preview, and refine interactive prototypes, live dashboards, slide decks, images, and motion graphics using custom design systems and coding agents.

### Main Capabilities
- **Agent-Native Runtimes:** Connects with mainstream coding agent CLIs—such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and DeepSeek Harness via native adapters, skills, CLI, or MCP servers.
- **Multimodal Studio Workspace:** Generates and previews web prototypes, live artifacts, HTML-based slide decks, images, and HTML-to-MP4 motion graphics through HyperFrames.
- **Brand-Grade Design Systems:** Standardizes visual styles using portable `DESIGN.md` contracts, token files, and bundled design-system packages.
- **Plugin and Skill Ecosystem:** Incorporates functional skills, design templates, and official plugins to support workflows like code migration and multi-format exports (HTML, PDF, PPTX, ZIP, MP4).

### Intended Users
Product managers, designers, and software engineers looking for a local-first, model-agnostic, and customizable collaborative workspace to generate and iterate on design artifacts via AI coding agents.

### Notable Technologies
TypeScript, Next.js, React, Node.js, Express, SQLite, Docker, Electron, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and HyperFrames.

name: material-ui
description: Material UI: Comprehensive React component library that implements Google's Material Design. Free forever.
summary: Material UI is a comprehensive library of React components featuring an independent implementation of Google's Material Design system. Designed for product teams and developers building user interfaces with React, it provides foundational UI building blocks and core functionality that can be extended with MUI X for advanced use cases.

name: app-ideas
description: A Collection of application ideas which can be used to improve your coding skills.
summary:
The App Ideas Collection repository provides a curated list of application projects designed to help developers improve coding skills, experiment with new technologies, and build out portfolios. Aimed at developers ranging from beginners to advanced practitioners, the repository helps overcome developer block by providing detailed specifications for building applications from the ground up. 

Each project specification includes a clear objective, user stories to guide implementation, optional bonus features, and helpful resources or links. Projects are categorized into three difficulty tiers: beginner-level user-facing applications, intermediate UI/UX and API integration apps, and advanced backend and database-backed applications. Examples span utilities, games, bots, and clones—such as a Bin2Dec converter, a Card Memory Game, a real-time Chat App, and a Discord Battleship Bot. The collection is structured to be extendable, encouraging contributors to submit new ideas and share completed implementations.

name: thefuck
description: Magnificent app which corrects your previous console command.
summary:
The Fuck is a console application designed to correct errors in previous command-line inputs. Intended for command-line users across various operating systems, it matches previous console commands with predefined or custom rules, generates the corrected command, and executes it (optionally with user confirmation). 

The application includes numerous built-in rules for popular tools and utilities such as git, apt, brew, docker, npm, python, and terraform, addressing typos, permission errors, missing arguments, and syntax mistakes. It also supports third-party rule packages, an experimental instant mode for faster execution in Bash or Zsh, and extensive configuration options via settings files or environment variables. 

The project is built using Python (version 3.5+) and requires pip and python-dev. Supported shells include Bash, Zsh, Fish, PowerShell, and tcsh.

name: tailwindcss
description: A utility-first CSS framework for rapid UI development.
summary: Tailwind CSS is a utility-first CSS framework designed for rapidly building custom user interfaces. It provides low-level utility classes that let developers construct bespoke designs directly in their markup without leaving HTML or writing custom CSS from scratch. Intended for web developers and designers, the framework focuses on speed, flexibility, and consistency in UI development.

name: autoresearch
description: AI agents running research on single-GPU nanochat training automatically
summary:
Autoresearch is an experimental framework designed to give an AI agent a small, single-GPU LLM training setup to conduct autonomous overnight machine learning research. The project allows an AI agent to iteratively modify a self-contained training script (`train.py`), evaluate performance using a fixed 5-minute time budget, and keep or discard changes based on validation bits per byte (`val_bpb`).

The core project workflow separates responsibilities: humans program the agent instructions and context using Markdown files (`program.md`), fixed data preparation and runtime evaluation utilities are handled by `prepare.py`, and the AI agent edits the model architecture, hyperparameters, optimizers, and training loop inside `train.py`.

Intended users are researchers and developers experimenting with autonomous AI agent loops for machine learning optimization. Notable technologies and libraries used include PyTorch, a Muon and AdamW optimizer setup, a BPE tokenizer, and the project manager `uv`, targeting a single NVIDIA GPU environment.

name: playwright
description: Playwright is a framework for Web Testing and Automation. It allows testing Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with a single API.
summary:
Playwright is a web automation and testing framework designed to drive Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit through a single unified API. It is built for end-to-end testing, browser automation scripts, web scraping, PDF generation, and LLM-driven AI agent integrations. 

Main capabilities include full browser isolation, auto-waiting, web-first assertions, resilient user-facing locators, storage state reuse, parallel test execution, and comprehensive execution tracing. It is accessible via multiple workflows: Playwright Test (a full-featured test runner), Playwright CLI (token-efficient command-line interface for coding agents), Playwright MCP (Model Context Protocol server for LLM-driven automation using accessibility snapshots), a core browser automation library, and a VS Code extension for test authoring, debugging, and code generation. 

Intended users include software testers, developers, and AI agents requiring programmatic or automated web browser control. Playwright supports cross-browser and cross-platform execution on Linux, macOS, and Windows, utilizing technologies such as Chrome for Testing, WebKit, and Firefox, with official language ports available for JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, .NET, and Java.

name: Deep-Live-Cam
description: real time face swap and one-click video deepfake with only a single image
summary: Deep-Live-Cam is a real-time face swap and video deepfake software designed for artists, creators, and media producers to animate custom characters, generate engaging content, and stream live performances using a single reference image. Intended users include digital artists, content creators, and streamers. Main capabilities comprise real-time webcam streaming, multiple face mapping, mouth masking for accurate expression retention, and image/video processing. Notable technologies utilized include Python, ONNX Runtime, OpenCV, PyTorch, InsightFace, GFPGAN, and FFmpeg, with support for execution providers such as CUDA, CoreML, DirectML, and OpenVINO.

name: Web-Dev-For-Beginners
description: 24 Lessons, 12 Weeks, Get Started as a Web Developer
summary:
Web Development for Beginners is a 12-week, project-based curriculum created by Microsoft Cloud Advocates to teach the fundamentals of web development. The course consists of 24 lessons covering JavaScript, CSS, and HTML through practical projects such as online terrariums, browser extensions, typing games, space games, and business banking apps, alongside new challenges involving GitHub Copilot and Generative AI. 

Intended for beginners, students, and educators, the curriculum emphasizes project-based pedagogy, pre- and post-lecture quizzes, knowledge checks, and assignments. Notable technologies and tools utilized throughout the course include JavaScript, HTML, CSS, GitHub, GitHub Copilot, Visual Studio Code, and the Canvas API.

name: paperclip
description: The open-source app everyone uses to manage agents at work
summary:
Paperclip is an open-source management application and control plane designed to orchestrate teams of AI agents to run a business. It functions as an agentic task manager, org chart, and operating system where users can assign business goals, define roles, and track work, progress, and costs from a unified dashboard. 

The platform supports multiple AI agent runtimes and harnesses—including OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Hermes, Grok, and Kimi Code—via external adapters or heartbeats. Its core architecture consists of four pillars: an Agentic Task Manager, an Org Chart for Agents (roles, permissions, and boundaries), Agent Employee Training (skills and evaluations), and an Agentic OS (runtime infrastructure, sandboxing, MCP servers, and cost controls). 

Paperclip is intended for teams, managers, IT professionals, and individuals who want to build autonomous AI organizations, run agents 24/7, monitor token spend and budgets, and manage multi-organization workflows without babysitting individual terminals. 

Notable technologies used include Node.js, React, TypeScript, and PostgreSQL.

name: bun
description: Incredibly fast JavaScript runtime, bundler, test runner, and package manager – all in one
summary:
Bun is an all-in-one JavaScript and TypeScript toolkit shipped as a single executable. Its core component is a fast JavaScript runtime designed as a drop-in replacement for Node.js, written in Rust and powered by JavaScriptCore to reduce startup times and memory usage. 

The project aims to provide comprehensive development tools for JavaScript and TypeScript developers, featuring an integrated test runner, script runner, bundler, and a Node.js-compatible package manager (`bun install` and `bunx`). It also exposes extensive native APIs for building HTTP and WebSocket servers, handling file I/O, managing SQLite, PostgreSQL, Redis, and S3 clients, and performing tasks like hashing, compression, and FFI integrations. 

Intended for JavaScript and TypeScript application developers, Bun supports Linux, macOS, and Windows environments, and integrates smoothly with common web frameworks and tooling like React, Next.js, Vite, and Prisma.

name: RuView
description: π RuView turns commodity WiFi signals into real-time spatial intelligence, vital sign monitoring, and presence detection — all without a single pixel of video.
summary:
**Project Purpose**  
π RuView is a spatial intelligence and WiFi sensing platform that converts standard radio frequency signals into actionable environmental and human activity data. By capturing Channel State Information (CSI) from low-cost edge hardware, the project enables camera-free tracking, vital sign monitoring, and room mapping without requiring visual equipment or wearables.

**Main Capabilities**  
- Detects human presence, occupancy counts, multi-room transitions, and entry/exit patterns through solid walls.  
- Monitors contactless vital signs, including continuous breathing and heart rate monitoring, sleep stages, and apnea/distress alerts.  
- Recognizes activities and motion dynamics such as walking, gestures, and fall detection.  
- Performs spatial RF fingerprinting, environment mapping, and 17-body keypoint pose estimation.  
- Integrates with major smart home platforms (Home Assistant via MQTT/HA-DISCO, Apple Home/HomePod via HAP-1.1, Google Home, and Amazon Alexa via Matter endpoints) and provides over 100 modular edge capabilities (cogs) for health, security, retail, and industrial use cases.

**Intended Users**  
The platform targets developers, smart home integrators, researchers, healthcare and assisted-living operators, and robotics engineers looking for privacy-preserving, through-wall, camera-free human monitoring and spatial intelligence solutions.

**Notable Technologies**  
- **Hardware:** ESP32-S3, ESP32-C6, and Raspberry Pi running edge sensing nodes.  
- **Languages & Frameworks:** Rust (v1.85+), Python (PyO3), TypeScript, and WebAssembly (Wasm).  
- **AI & Processing:** Spiking neural networks, contrastive encoders, HuBERT/Candle-based models, and RuVector for persistent memory and vector storage.  
- **Protocols & Integrations:** MQTT, HAP-1.1, Matter, and Model Context Protocol (MCP).

name: awesome-mcp-servers
description: A collection of MCP servers.

name: puppeteer
description: JavaScript API for Chrome and Firefox
summary: Puppeteer is a JavaScript library that provides a high-level API to control Chrome or Firefox. It operates primarily in headless mode by default and communicates using the DevTools Protocol or WebDriver BiDi. Designed for web developers, testers, and automation engineers, Puppeteer enables capabilities such as browser automation, page navigation, user interaction simulation, screen sizing, and debugging. The project supports packages like `puppeteer` and `puppeteer-core`, integrates with MCP servers such as `chrome-devtools-mcp`, and includes support for the experimental WebMCP API.

name: claude-mem
description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent –  Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More
summary:
Claude-Mem is a persistent memory compression system built for Claude Code and compatible with various IDEs and agent harnesses, such as Grok Bot, OpenCode, Antigravity CLI, Oh My Pi, and OpenClaw gateways. It seamlessly preserves context across sessions by automatically capturing tool usage observations, generating semantic summaries, and providing them to future sessions to maintain continuity of project knowledge.

Main capabilities include progressive disclosure, a skill-based search workflow utilizing four MCP tools (`search`, `timeline`, `get_observations`), a real-time web viewer UI, cloud sync options, and hybrid semantic and keyword search. It supports privacy controls via `<private>` tags, multiple workflow modes, and language configurations. 

Intended for developers and AI agent users, the project is written in TypeScript and managed using Node.js (>=20.0.0), Bun, and Python's `uv`. It relies on a local SQLite 3 database for storage, Chroma for vector database operations, and implements its core functionality through session lifecycle hooks.

name: nvm
description: Node Version Manager - POSIX-compliant bash script to manage multiple active node.js versions.
summary: Node Version Manager (nvm) is a command-line tool for POSIX-compliant shells (such as sh, dash, ksh, zsh, and bash) that allows users to quickly install, manage, and switch between multiple versions of Node.js and io.js per-user and per-shell. Designed for developers working on Unix, macOS, Windows WSL, and Linux systems (including Alpine Linux), nvm enables setting default Node versions, managing long-term support (LTS) releases, migrating global packages between versions, executing commands in subshells via specific versions, and referencing versions automatically using `.nvmrc` configuration files. Notable features include offline installation support, custom shell completion, colorized output customization, binary mirror support, and execution via command-line flags or install scripts.

name: clean-code-javascript
description: Clean Code concepts adapted for JavaScript
summary:
Clean Code JavaScript adapts software engineering principles from Robert C. Martin’s book _Clean Code_ for JavaScript developers. The project serves as a comprehensive guide for producing readable, reusable, and refactorable software rather than acting as a strict style guide. 

The guide covers multiple aspects of software craftsmanship, including variables, functions, objects and data structures, classes, SOLID design principles, testing, concurrency, error handling, formatting, and comments. It provides practical "bad" versus "good" code examples for concepts such as using meaningful and searchable variable names, keeping functions small with limited arguments, favoring functional programming and composition, handling asynchronous operations with Promises and Async/Await, and utilizing ES2015/ES6 classes and features. 

The intended users are JavaScript developers and software engineering teams seeking to assess and improve the quality of their codebase. Notable technologies and concepts referenced include JavaScript (ES5, ES2015/ES6, ES2017/ES8), TypeScript, ESLint, MomentJS, and asynchronous programming primitives.

name: java-design-patterns
description: Design patterns implemented in Java
summary:
This repository showcases a comprehensive collection of software design patterns implemented in Java. Developed by experienced programmers and architects from the open-source community, the project provides well-commented source code examples and high-level descriptions that serve as practical programming tutorials. 

The main capabilities of the repository include browsing design patterns by name, tags (such as `Performance`, `Gang of Four`, or `Data access`), or categories like `Creational` and `Behavioral`. It is intended for software developers, architects, and coders seeking to learn and apply proven development paradigms, improve code readability, and prevent common architectural issues when designing applications and systems. 

The project emphasizes object-oriented solutions built using popular, battle-proven open-source Java technologies and adheres to software design principles such as KISS, YAGNI, and principles of practical extensibility.

name: manim
description: Animation engine for explanatory math videos
summary:
Manim (specifically the `manimgl` package) is an engine for precise programmatic animations designed for creating explanatory math videos. Originally created as a personal project for the author of 3Blue1Brown, the library provides tools to render mathematical scenes, shapes, and text through Python code. 

The software targets content creators, educators, and developers interested in mathematical visualization. Notable technologies and dependencies utilized by Manim include Python (version 3.10 or higher), FFmpeg for video processing, OpenGL for rendering, LaTeX for mathematical typesetting, and Pango for text layout on Linux systems.

name: Stirling-PDF
description: #1 PDF Application on GitHub that lets you edit PDFs on any device anywhere
summary:
Stirling-PDF is an open-source PDF platform designed for editing, signing, redacting, converting, and automating PDF documents without relying on external services. It can be used as a personal desktop application, accessed via a browser UI, or deployed on local servers with a private API. 

Key capabilities include over 50 PDF tools (such as merging, splitting, OCR, and compression), no-code automation pipelines within the UI, enterprise-grade features like Single Sign-On (SSO) and auditing, REST APIs for system integration, and a global user interface available in over 40 languages. The project targets individual users, developers, and enterprises seeking self-hosted or on-premise document processing solutions. Technologies utilized include Docker, Kubernetes, and Task as a command runner for building, developing, and testing.

name: localsend
description: An open-source cross-platform alternative to AirDrop
summary:
LocalSend is a free, open-source, cross-platform application designed to securely share files and messages with nearby devices over a local network without requiring an internet connection or third-party servers. 

Intended for general users seeking direct local communication, the project implements a secure communication protocol using a REST API and HTTPS encryption, with TLS/SSL certificates generated dynamically on each device. It includes both a graphical cross-platform app and a terminal-based command-line interface (CLI) client built on the LocalSend Protocol v2. 

The application is built using Flutter and Rust, utilizing FVM (Flutter Version Management) for version consistency. It supports Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS, and Fire OS platforms, communicating primarily over TCP/UDP port 53317.

name: sherlock
description: Hunt down social media accounts by username across social networks
summary: Sherlock is a command-line tool designed to hunt down social media accounts by username across more than 400 social networks. Its main capabilities include checking single or multiple usernames concurrently, searching similar username variations, routing requests through proxies, and exporting results in various formats such as text files, CSV, JSON, and XLSX. The tool is intended for security researchers, investigators, and individuals performing open-source intelligence (OSINT). Sherlock is distributed as a Python package installable via `pipx`, `pip`, `uv`, or Docker, with community-maintained packages available for platforms like Debian, Ubuntu, Homebrew, Kali, and BlackArch.

name: vllm
description: A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs
summary:
vLLM is a fast, flexible library designed for Large Language Model (LLM) inference and serving. It delivers state-of-the-art serving throughput through features such as PagedAttention for efficient attention key and value memory management, continuous batching, chunked prefill, prefix caching, CUDA/HIP graphs, speculative decoding, and diverse quantization formats (including FP8, INT8/INT4, GPTQ, AWQ, and GGUF). 

The platform supports over 200 Hugging Face model architectures—including decoder-only LLMs, Mixture-of-Experts, multi-modal models, embedding and retrieval models, and reward models. It offers distributed inference using tensor, pipeline, data, expert, and context parallelism, multi-LoRA support, streaming outputs, structured outputs via xgrammar or guidance, tool calling, and an OpenAI-compatible API server with gRPC support. 

Intended for developers and researchers deploying LLMs, vLLM supports NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs, x86/ARM/PowerPC CPUs, and hardware accelerators like Google TPUs, Intel Gaudi, Huawei Ascend, and Apple Silicon. Notable technologies utilized include FlashAttention, FlashInfer, Triton, CUTLASS, and torch.compile.

name: taste-skill
description: Taste-Skill - gives your AI good taste. stops the AI from generating boring, generic slop
summary:
Taste Skill is an anti-slop frontend framework providing portable Agent Skills designed to upgrade AI-built user interfaces with improved layout, typography, motion, and spacing. It offers specialized implementation skills (such as `design-taste-frontend`, `gpt-taste`, `image-to-code`, `redesign-existing-projects`, and `minimalist-ui`) that output clean code, alongside image-generation skills (`imagegen-frontend-web`, `imagegen-frontend-mobile`, and `brandkit`) that produce reference design boards. 

Intended for developers and AI agents utilizing coding tools like Codex, Cursor, Claude Code, and ChatGPT, the framework emphasizes high visual quality and framework-agnostic design rules. Notable technologies and tools referenced include GSAP for motion, React, Vue, Svelte, and the `npx skills add` CLI for installation.

name: uptime-kuma
description: A fancy self-hosted monitoring tool
summary:
Uptime Kuma is an easy-to-use, self-hosted monitoring tool designed to track the operational status and uptime of various services. 

Main capabilities include monitoring uptime for HTTP(s), TCP, HTTP(s) Keyword, HTTP(s) Json Query, WebSockets, Ping, DNS records, Push, Steam game servers, and Docker containers. It features 20-second check intervals, ping charts, certificate information, proxy support, two-factor authentication (2FA), multiple customizable status pages that can map to specific domains, and over 90 notification services such as Telegram, Discord, Gotify, Slack, Pushover, and SMTP email.

The project provides a reactive and fast user interface and supports multiple languages. It can be installed via Docker Compose, a Docker command, or natively on major Linux distributions and Windows using Node.js, Git, and PM2. Notable technologies and frameworks used include Vue 3, Vite.js, Bootstrap 5, WebSockets, and Docker.

name: DeepSeek-R1
summary:
DeepSeek-R1 is a collection of open-source reasoning models developed by DeepSeek-AI, including DeepSeek-R1-Zero, DeepSeek-R1, and several distilled dense models based on the Qwen and Llama architectures. 

The project's primary purpose is to incentivize advanced reasoning capabilities in large language models using large-scale reinforcement learning (RL) without relying solely on supervised fine-tuning. DeepSeek-R1-Zero develops reasoning behaviors like self-verification and chain-of-thought (CoT) generation purely through RL, while DeepSeek-R1 integrates cold-start data and multi-stage RL and supervised fine-tuning pipelines to achieve performance comparable to OpenAI-o1 on math, coding, and reasoning tasks. Additionally, the repository provides distilled smaller models (ranging from 1.5B to 70B parameters) trained on reasoning data generated by DeepSeek-R1.

The models are intended for researchers, developers, and the broader AI community seeking high-performance reasoning LLMs for local deployment, commercial applications, or further model distillation. Notable technologies used include Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, Hugging Face, vLLM, and SGLang. The models are released under the MIT License, though specific distilled variants inherit terms from their respective base models.

name: ragflow
description: RAGFlow is a leading open-source Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) engine that fuses cutting-edge RAG with Agent capabilities to create a superior context layer for LLMs
summary:
RAGFlow is an open-source Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) engine that combines RAG with agent capabilities to provide a context layer for large language models. It is designed for developers and enterprises seeking to transform unstructured data into production-ready AI systems.

Main capabilities include deep document understanding for complex unstructured formats, template-based chunking, Knowledge Compilation (generating Wikis, Graphs, Trees, PageIndex, Mind Maps, Timelines, and Skills), Agentic Retrieval with multi-step reasoning and thinking modes, grounded citations, heterogeneous data source compatibility (including Word, Excel, slides, images, web pages, and Google BigQuery), and automated RAG workflows. 

The system utilizes a Go-native service architecture encompassing an API, Admin, Ingestor, and Syncer, alongside DeepDoc for layout analysis, OCR, and table recognition via CGO and ONNX Runtime. Deployment options include Docker containers and building from source with dependencies like MySQL, MinIO, NATS, Kvrocks, ClickHouse, and Elasticsearch or Infinity.

name: OpenCut
description: The open-source CapCut alternative
summary: OpenCut is a free and open-source video editor designed for web, desktop, and mobile platforms. The project is currently being rewritten from the ground up featuring a plugin-first architecture, a Rust core, an Editor API, first-class third-party plugins, a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI agents, a headless mode for automation and batch rendering, and an integrated scripting tab. The repository utilizes proto and moon for development management.

name: zed
description: Code at the speed of thought – Zed is a high-performance, multiplayer code editor from the creators of Atom and Tree-sitter.
summary: Zed is a high-performance, multiplayer code editor created by the developers of Atom and Tree-sitter. Developed by Zed Industries, Inc., it is designed for software developers and engineers seeking a fast, collaborative coding environment. The editor supports macOS, Linux, and Windows platforms. The source code is licensed primarily under GPL-3.0-or-later, with select components under Apache-2.0, and utilizes Cargo and `cargo-about` for dependency and open-source license management.

name: django
description: The Web framework for perfectionists with deadlines.
summary: Django is a high-level Python web framework designed to encourage rapid development and clean, pragmatic design. It provides structured documentation for installation, tutorials, deployment, topical guides, and references, along with a built-in test suite for verifying code contributions.

name: core
description: :house_with_garden: Open source home automation that puts local control and privacy first.
summary:
Home Assistant is an open-source home automation system that prioritizes local control and privacy. Designed to run on a Raspberry Pi or a local server, the project is powered by a worldwide community of tinkerers and DIY enthusiasts. 

The system features a modular architecture that allows users to easily implement support for various devices and actions, enabling custom component creation.

name: ML-For-Beginners
description: 12 weeks, 26 lessons, 52 quizzes, classic Machine Learning for all
summary:
This repository contains a 12-week, 26-lesson open-source curriculum titled "Machine Learning for Beginners," created by Microsoft Cloud Advocates. The project is designed to teach students and beginners the fundamentals of classic machine learning through a project-based pedagogy, featuring global cultural themes, pre- and post-lesson quizzes, step-by-step instructions, assignments, and knowledge checks. 

The curriculum covers core topics such as regression, classification, clustering, natural language processing (NLP), time series forecasting, and reinforcement learning. Intended users include students, self-taught learners, and teachers seeking structured educational materials. 

Notable technologies and libraries utilized throughout the course include Python, Scikit-learn, R (via R Markdown files), GitHub Codespaces, Docsify, and various machine learning models and techniques like linear/logistic regression, K-Means clustering, ARIMA, Support Vector Regressor (SVR), and Q-Learning.

name: storybook
description: Storybook is the industry standard workshop for building, documenting, and testing UI components in isolation
summary:
Storybook is a frontend workshop designed for building UI components and pages in isolation. It is utilized by development teams for UI development, testing, and documentation. 

Main capabilities include component design, documentation, interactivity, and extension via an API and various addons such as accessibility testing (a11y), actions, backgrounds, docs, links, measurements, outlines, and viewports. 

Intended users include frontend and mobile developers working across multiple frameworks. Notable technologies and supported frameworks include React, Angular, Vue 3, Web Components, React Native, HTML, Ember, Svelte, Preact, Qwik, SolidJS, Android, iOS, and Flutter.

name: opencv
description: Open Source Computer Vision Library
summary: OpenCV (Open Source Computer Vision Library) is an open-source library providing a comprehensive set of infrastructure and tools for computer vision and AI development. The project serves developers and researchers working in computer vision by offering core algorithmic capabilities, documentation, and a dedicated Q&A forum. Additional specialized functionality is available through the companion opencv_contrib repository.

name: servers
description: Model Context Protocol Servers
summary:
This repository contains reference implementations of servers for the Model Context Protocol (MCP), designed to give Large Language Models (LLMs) secure, controlled access to external tools and data sources. It provides educational examples demonstrating MCP features, SDK usage, and server extensibility. 

The repository includes active reference servers such as Everything, Fetch, Filesystem, Git, Memory, Sequential Thinking, and Time, alongside various archived implementations like AWS KB Retrieval, Brave Search, EverArt, GitHub, GitLab, Google Drive, Google Maps, PostgreSQL, Puppeteer, Redis, Sentry, Slack, and SQLite. 

Intended for developers building their own MCP servers or configuring MCP clients (such as Claude Desktop), the repository showcases integrations built with official MCP SDKs available in C#, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, Swift, and TypeScript. Setup utilities utilize tools like `npx` and `uvx`.

name: PaddleOCR
description: Turn any PDF or image document into structured data for your AI. A powerful, lightweight OCR toolkit that bridges the gap between images/PDFs and LLMs. Supports 100+ languages.
summary:
PaddleOCR is a global leading optical character recognition (OCR) toolkit and document AI engine designed to convert PDF documents and images into structured, LLM-ready data such as JSON and Markdown. 

Main capabilities include intelligent document parsing via vision-language models like PaddleOCR-VL and PP-StructureV3 for structure-aware conversion, alongside universal scene text recognition supporting over 100 languages through PP-OCR series models. The project provides high-throughput document parsing, complex element mastery (such as tables, formulas, charts, and seals), a complete data engine for LLM fine-tuning, and robust deployment utilities.

Intended users include developers, researchers, and engineers building intelligent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Agentic applications. 

Notable technologies and frameworks used include PaddlePaddle, PP-OCR, PP-StructureV3, PaddleOCR-VL, HPD-Parsing, Python, C++, ONNX, OpenVINO, TensorRT, vLLM, and Hugging Face Transformers, with deployment support across Linux, Windows, macOS, CPU, GPU, XPU, and NPU hardware.

name: mermaid
description: Generation of diagrams like flowcharts or sequence diagrams from text in a similar manner as markdown
summary:
