The project's main capabilities include a robust command-line interface, support for exporting and importing configuration settings, and advanced administrative features such as modifying other Windows user accounts and supporting Windows Audit/Sysprep mode for default user profile customization. 

Intended users include standard Windows users looking to optimize their operating system, as well as power users and system administrators. The project relies on PowerShell as its core technology.

name: twenty
description: The open alternative to Salesforce, designed for AI.
summary:
Twenty is an open-source CRM designed for technical teams to build, ship, and version custom customer relationship management solutions. It provides foundational building blocks such as objects, custom views, workflows, layouts, AI agents, and chat capabilities. Users can define objects, fields, and views as code using the Twenty CLI (`create-twenty-app`) and publish apps directly to their workspaces with version control. 

Intended users are technical teams, developers, and organizations seeking customizable, extensible, and self-hostable CRM infrastructure. 

The project is built using TypeScript, Nx, NestJS, PostgreSQL, Redis, BullMQ, React, Jotai, Linaria, and Lingui. It supports cloud deployment, self-hosting via Docker Compose, and local development setups.

name: awesome-android-ui
description: A curated list of awesome Android UI/UX libraries
summary: This repository provides a curated list of Android UI and UX libraries, designed to help developers build and enhance user interfaces. It categorizes a wide variety of open-source tools and components, covering Jetpack Compose, layouts, buttons, lists and grids, viewpagers, labels and forms, images, seekbars, progress indicators, menus, action bars, dialogs, calendars, graphs, animations, parallax effects, visual effects, and other utility components. The collection highlights specific projects such as Landscapist, MPAndroidChart, Lottie for Android, and Material Dialogs, providing developers with readily accessible options for modern Android application design and implementation.

name: jellyfin
description: The Free Software Media System - Server Backend & API
summary:
Jellyfin is a free software media system designed to give users full control over managing and streaming their media collections from a dedicated server to end-user devices via multiple applications. Serving as an alternative to proprietary solutions like Emby and Plex, Jellyfin is descended from Emby's 3.5.2 release and has been ported to the .NET platform for cross-platform support.

This repository contains the backend server code. The project is intended for users seeking a self-hosted media streaming solution and developers looking to contribute to the media system. 

Notable technologies and prerequisites used in the project include:
- **.NET 10 SDK** (and .NET-compatible IDEs such as Visual Studio and Visual Studio Code)
- **FFmpeg** for media processing and transcoding
- **jellyfin-web** for the frontend web client interface

name: DeepLearning-500-questions
description: 深度学习500问，以问答形式对常用的概率知识、线性代数、机器学习、深度学习、计算机视觉等热点问题进行阐述，以帮助自己及有需要的读者。 全书分为18个章节，50余万字。由于水平有限，书中不妥之处恳请广大读者批评指正。   未完待续............ 如有意合作，联系scutjy2015@163.com                     版权所有，违权必究       Tan 2018.06
summary:
《深度学习500问——AI工程师面试宝典》系统梳理了深度学习的基本理论、核心算法及其在计算机视觉等领域的应用。本书主要内容涵盖数学基础、机器学习基础、深度学习基础、经典网络结构（如CNN、RNN、GAN）、目标检测与图像分割等视觉应用，以及迁移学习、网络优化、超参数调整和模型压缩加速等高级主题。

本书面向高等院校计算机科学、人工智能及相关专业的研究与教学人员、本科生和研究生，同时也是深度学习与计算机视觉初中级研究人员、工程技术人员、求职应聘者以及相关岗位面试官的理想参考资料。

name: html5-boilerplate
description: A professional front-end template for building fast, robust, and adaptable web apps or sites.
summary: HTML5 Boilerplate is a professional front-end template designed for building fast, robust, and adaptable web apps and sites without imposing a specific development philosophy or framework. Its main capabilities include progressive enhancement design, placeholder Open Graph elements, CSS media queries, helper classes, and performance-optimized default print styles. It also includes an example `package.json` file featuring built-in Webpack commands. The project is intended for web developers and designers looking for a quick-start starter template that supports the latest, stable releases of all major browsers according to Browserslist defaults. Notable technologies referenced include HTML5, Webpack, npm, yarn, and Gulp (used for project production).

name: faceswap
description: Deepfakes Software For All
summary:
FaceSwap is a Python-based deep learning tool designed to recognize and swap faces in pictures and videos. The software provides a structured pipeline consisting of extraction, model training, and conversion stages, accessible via a command-line interface or a graphical user interface (GUI). It is intended for ethical uses such as AI experimentation, educational learning, social or political commentary, and movie production. 

The project targets developers, researchers, hobbyists, and advanced users interested in computer vision and generative AI models. For optimal performance, it requires a modern GPU with CUDA support or AMD ROCm on Linux. Notable technical components and dependencies mentioned include Python, OpenCV, FFmpeg, CUDA, ROCm, as well as specific neural network models and aligners like FAN and MTCNN.

name: private-gpt
description: Complete API layer for private AI applications on local models: RAG, skills, tools, MCP, text-to-sql, and more. Works with any OpenAI-compatible inference server.
summary:
PrivateGPT is an open-source, API-first application layer designed to turn local models into production-ready AI applications without depending on cloud APIs. It connects to any OpenAI-compatible inference server—such as Ollama, llama.cpp, or vLLM—to supply higher-level backend primitives and an Anthropic/Claude-compatible API model. 

Its main capabilities include a standard messages API with streaming and token counting, file and artifact ingestion, document retrieval with citations, agentic RAG, and built-in tools for web search, web extraction, code execution, database querying, tabular/CSV analysis, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectors. It also includes a built-in workbench UI for testing and demos.

Intended for developers building self-hosted AI products, local agents, and workflows, PrivateGPT integrates natively with tools like Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Microsoft 365 add-ins, n8n, OpenCode, and VS Code. Notable technologies leveraged include Python, uv, Ollama, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

name: appwrite
description: Appwrite® - complete cloud infrastructure for your web, mobile and AI apps. Including Auth, Databases, Storage, Functions, Messaging, Hosting, Realtime and more
summary:
Appwrite is an open-source, MCP and agent-first cloud platform designed for building and scaling applications and operating on live projects via AI agents. Targeted at both developers and AI workflows, it delivers modular backend products including Auth, Databases, Storage, Functions, Sites, Messaging, Firewall, Realtime, and MCP integration. 

The platform supports self-hosting via Docker on Unix and Windows, cloud marketplaces like DigitalOcean, AWS, and Akamai, and offers a managed cloud alternative. It provides extensive client and server SDKs across numerous languages and frameworks such as Web, Flutter, React, Node.js, Python, and Go. Appwrite features a hybrid monolithic-microservice architecture that supports REST, WebSocket, and GraphQL APIs alongside in-memory caching and background workers.

name: ppt-master
description: AI turns documents or topics into real, native PowerPoint decks—with native shapes, transitions and animations, data-backed charts and tables on demand, audio narration from speaker notes, and support for your own .pptx templates. · by Hugo He
summary:
PPT Master is an open-source workflow and AI agent skill that generates natively editable PowerPoint presentations (.pptx) from any source document, such as PDFs, DOCX files, web pages, or text prompts. 

The project's primary purpose is to produce truly editable PowerPoint decks rather than flat images or static templates, utilizing native objects such as slide masters, layouts, shapes, connectors, data-backed charts, tables, and OMML formulas. It can also distill templates, fill existing .pptx files with new content, and add animations, transitions, or narration.

Intended users include professionals, researchers, developers, and finance practitioners who frequently create or review presentation decks and want to leverage AI without sacrificing local data privacy or PowerPoint editability.

PPT Master runs locally on the user's machine inside any agent-capable AI environment (such as Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, or Cline) and supports multiple AI models and relay platforms. Notable technologies utilized include Python, PyMuPDF, Pandoc (for legacy formats), and various AI vision and text models (with recommendations including Kimi K3, Claude, and specialized image generation backends like `gpt-image-2` or Google `gemini-3.1-flash-image`).

name: rich
description: Rich is a Python library for rich text and beautiful formatting in the terminal.
summary:
Rich is a Python library designed for rich text formatting and appealing terminal output. It enables developers and command-line application users to effortlessly add color, styles, word-wrapping, and structure to standard console prints, logs, and REPL sessions. 

Main capabilities include rendering pretty tables, flicker-free progress bars, activity spinners, hierarchical trees, data columns, markdown documents, syntax-highlighted source code via Pygments, and beautiful, readable tracebacks. It also provides a logging handler to format and colorize outputs from Python's standard logging module. 

Rich is compatible with Linux, macOS, and Windows—supporting true color and emojis on modern terminals like Windows Terminal—and integrates natively with Jupyter notebooks. It requires Python 3.8 or later.

name: n8n-workflows
description: all of the workflows of n8n i could find (also from the site itself)
summary:
The n8n Workflow Collection provides an ultimate repository of over 4,343 production-ready n8n automation workflows featuring 365+ unique integrations across 15 organized categories. It is designed for developers, system administrators, and automation engineers looking to discover, search, and download pre-built workflow JSON files for marketing, sales, DevOps, and other use cases. 

The project features a high-performance web interface backed by a FastAPI server and an SQLite database utilizing FTS5 for sub-100ms full-text search capabilities. Users can access the searchable collection online via GitHub Pages or host the application locally using Python 3.9+ or Docker containers with multi-platform support (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64). Notable technologies used include Python, FastAPI, SQLite FTS5, Vanilla JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, Docker, and GitHub Actions.

name: you-get
description: :arrow_double_down: Dumb downloader that scrapes the web

name: fuel-core
description: Rust full node implementation of the Fuel v2 protocol.
summary:
Fuel Client (`fuel-core`) is a Rust-based client implementation for the Fuel network, designed for node operators, developers, and network participants across networks like Fuel Ignition, Testnet, and Devnet. 

The project provides capabilities to run, build, and configure a Fuel node locally or within networks such as Ignition, support local testnet configuration, execute transactions, and provide a GraphQL service endpoint (`/v1/graphql`) for interacting with the client and submitting transactions. Key technical components and dependencies include Rust, WASM targets, RocksDB for state persistence, and GraphQL schemas for client queries and mutations.

name: face_recognition
description: The world's simplest facial recognition api for Python and the command line
summary:
Face Recognition is a Python and command-line library designed to recognize and manipulate human faces. Built using dlib and deep learning, the model achieves high accuracy on facial recognition benchmarks. 

Its primary capabilities include:
- Finding face locations in pictures.
- Locating and outlining facial features (such as eyes, nose, mouth, and chin) for tasks like digital make-up.
- Identifying and recognizing specific individuals in photographs, videos, or real-time webcam streams.
- Providing command-line tools for batch face detection and recognition.

The library is intended for developers, researchers, and hobbyists working on computer vision and machine learning applications. It supports integration with other Python libraries such as OpenCV, Flask, NumPy, and SciPy, and can be deployed via Docker containers on hardware ranging from standard PCs to Raspberry Pi and Nvidia Jetson Nano boards.

name: project-layout
description: Standard Go Project Layout
summary:
This repository provides a standard project layout and common pattern guidelines for Go application projects. It is a community-driven set of historical and emerging project structure patterns rather than an official standard defined by the core Go dev team. The project aims to help developers organize growing Go codebases, applications, and libraries effectively by proposing common directories for different purposes.

Key components and directory patterns described include:
- `/cmd`: Main applications for the project, where each application directory matches its executable name.
- `/internal`: Private application and library code enforced as non-importable by external projects via the Go compiler.
- `/pkg`: Library code that is safe for use by external applications.
- `/vendor`: Application dependencies managed manually or via Go Modules.
- Additional common directories for operational needs, such as `/api`, `/web`, `/configs`, `/init`, `/scripts`, `/build`, `/deployments`, `/test`, `/docs`, `/tools`, and `/examples`.

The guide is intended for Go developers structuring real-world applications and larger projects, while noting that it may be an overkill for simple proofs-of-concept or single-file scripts. Notable technologies and tools referenced include Go Modules, OpenAPI, Swagger, systemd, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, `gofmt`, and `staticcheck`.

name: react-router
description: Declarative routing for React
summary: React Router is a multi-strategy router for React that functions either as a full React framework or minimally as a library integrated into custom architectures. It provides routing capabilities for React applications across various environments and platforms. The repository includes packages such as `react-router`, `create-react-router`, `@react-router/dev`, `@react-router/node`, `@react-router/serve`, `@react-router/express`, `@react-router/architect`, `@react-router/cloudflare`, and `@react-router/fs-routes`. Technologies and platforms explicitly mentioned include React, Node.js, Express, Architect, and Cloudflare.

name: joplin
description: Joplin - the privacy-focused note taking app with sync capabilities for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS.
summary:
Joplin is a free, open-source, offline-first note-taking and to-do application designed to handle large volumes of notes organized into searchable notebooks. Notes are written in Markdown format and can be tagged, copied, modified, and synchronized across devices using end-to-end encryption with cloud services such as Nextcloud, Dropbox, OneDrive, and Joplin Cloud. 

The application is targeted at users seeking a secure, self-contained note-taking solution with full-text search capabilities across all platforms. Notable features include the ability to import complete metadata and formatted content from Evernote, support for plugins and themes for customization, and a Web Clipper extension available for Firefox and Chrome to save web pages and screenshots directly from a browser. Joplin is available for Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, and iOS.

name: free-claude-code
description: Use Claude Code, Codex, VSCode, Pi, and OpenCode (and 6 other harnesses) for free (1.3B+ free tokens) from your terminal, app, IDE, or phone, and now from the browser with native browser sessions (multi-harness + multi-model) like OpenClaw (voice supported + ToS friendly)
summary:
Free Claude Code (FCC) is an independent open-source project that serves as a searchable unified UI and proxy for 59 ToS-friendly AI providers—offering over 1.3 billion free tokens monthly, subscription access, paid models, and local models. It supports 11 coding agents, including Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, Cline, Hermes, DeepSeek Harness, Grok Build, Muse Code, Aider, and VS Code Chat. 

Designed for developers, FCC enables users to continue coding uninterrupted through provider outages via automatic model failover, reduces terminal output tokens by up to 90%, runs native browser code sessions with real-time support, and provides voice note transcription via local Whisper or NVIDIA NIM. It integrates across terminal, desktop, IDE, phone, Discord, and Telegram clients. Notable technologies used include Python 3.14, uv, Pytest, Ty, Ruff, and Loguru.

name: typst
description: A markup-based typesetting system that is powerful and easy to learn.
summary:
Typst is a markup-based typesetting system designed to match the power of LaTeX while remaining easy to learn and use. It provides built-in markup, flexible formatting functions, a tightly integrated scripting system, math typesetting, and bibliography management. The system prioritizes fast compile times through incremental compilation using `comemo`, along with friendly error messages. 

This repository contains the Typst compiler and its command-line interface (CLI) for local document compilation, supporting actions such as building, watching files for automatic recompilation, and managing custom font paths. The project is intended for writers, researchers, and developers seeking a modern, consistent, and composable typesetting workflow. Typst is written in Rust and adheres to design principles focusing on simplicity, composability, and incremental performance.

name: hyperframes
description: Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.
summary:
HyperFrames is an open-source framework and rendering engine designed for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Built for AI coding agents and automated workflows, it provides a CLI, agent skills, and a design system called `frame.md` that translates web design tokens into video-optimized formats. 

Main capabilities include local and cloud-based rendering (via AWS Lambda), live browser previews with hot-reload, audio mixing, and a catalog of reusable blocks and components like charts and transitions. It supports multiple animation runtimes, including GSAP, CSS, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, and WAAPI. 

Intended users include developers, creators, and teams building automated video pipelines, product launch videos, PR walkthroughs, data visualizations, and motion graphics. Notable technologies and tools used across the stack include Node.js 22+, FFmpeg, Puppeteer, Git LFS, and Headless Chrome.

name: voicebox
description: The open-source AI voice studio. Clone, dictate, create.
summary:
Voicebox is an open-source, local-first AI voice studio designed to provide a privacy-focused alternative to cloud voice platforms like ElevenLabs and WisprFlow. It integrates a complete voice input/output stack with a bundled local LLM for text refinement and customizable profile personas.

Main capabilities include zero-shot voice cloning and preset voice generation across 7 text-to-speech (TTS) engines (such as Qwen3-TTS, LuxTTS, Chatterbox, HumeAI TADA, and Kokoro) in 23 languages, unlimited text generation with auto-chunking and crossfading, multi-track audio editing via a stories editor, post-processing audio effects powered by Spotify's `pedalboard`, and speech-to-text transcription via Whisper. It also features global system-wide dictation with target-aware auto-paste, agent voice output through a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, and a REST API.

Intended users include developers, creators, and individuals seeking local voice generation, dictation, and voice-enabled AI agent workflows. Notable technologies used include Tauri (Rust) for desktop app performance, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Python (FastAPI), PyTorch, MLX for Apple Silicon, SQLite, and Spotify's Pedalboard.

name: first-contributions
description: 🚀✨ Help beginners to contribute to open source projects
summary:
The **First Contributions** project simplifies and guides beginners through the standard open-source workflow of making their first code contribution. It is designed for beginner developers and newcomers looking to learn Git and GitHub basics, such as forking repositories, cloning, creating branches, committing changes, and submitting pull requests. 

The repository provides step-by-step instructions utilizing command-line Git commands (such as `git clone`, `git switch`, `git add`, `git commit`, and `git push`), alongside alternative tutorials using graphical user interface tools like GitHub Desktop, Visual Studio Code, GitKraken, Sourcetree, Visual Studio 2017, and IntelliJ IDEA. Notable technologies and tools involved include Git, GitHub, and Markdown files (`Contributors.md`).

name: Motrix
description: A full-featured download manager.
summary:
Motrix is a modern, full-featured desktop download manager and headless server designed to handle HTTP, FTP, BitTorrent, and magnet links while maintaining a clean and intuitive user experience. 

The project features a decoupled UI and download core, enabling two operational modes: a cross-platform desktop application for macOS, Windows, and Linux, and a headless server deployable via Node.js or Docker for NAS devices and home servers. Browser extensions, command-line tools, and plugins interact with the core via **MDXP** (Motrix Download eXchange Protocol), a JSON-RPC 2.0-based protocol.

Key capabilities include SQLite-backed session persistence, BitTorrent support with per-file selection, UPnP/NAT-PMP port mapping, speed-limit profiles, system notifications, a customizable dashboard, and QuickJS-based sandboxed plugin support. 

Notable technologies used in the stack include Electron, React 19, Tailwind CSS, TypeScript, Vite, Zod, better-sqlite3, QuickJS, Fastify, and a Motrix-maintained fork of aria2 as the download engine. Quality and development are supported using Biome, Vitest, and Playwright.

name: gatsby
description: React-based framework with performance, scalability, and security built in.
summary:
Gatsby is a free and open-source web development framework based on React, designed to help professional developers efficiently build fast, maintainable, content-rich websites and applications. 

Main capabilities include pulling data from any source—such as Markdown files, headless CMS platforms like Contentful or WordPress, and REST or GraphQL APIs—via a uniform GraphQL interface. Gatsby supports multiple rendering options on a per-page basis, including Static Site Generation (SSG), Deferred Static Generation (DSG), and Server-Side Rendering (SSR). It automatically handles performance optimizations like code splitting, image optimization, critical style inlining, lazy-loading, and resource prefetching. Sites can be hosted cost-effectively on CDNs without requiring dedicated servers.

Intended users are professional developers and development teams seeking a modern React and GraphQL stack to create dynamic applications ranging from blogs and e-commerce sites to user dashboards. Notable technologies utilized include React, GraphQL, Lerna for monorepo management, and integration support with deployment platforms like Netlify.

name: leetcode
description: LeetCode Solutions: A Record of My Problem Solving Journey.( leetcode题解，记录自己的leetcode解题之路。)
summary:
This repository provides comprehensive LeetCode problem solutions, data structures and algorithms summaries, and study guides aimed at software engineers and developers preparing for technical interviews. The project purpose is to help users master foundational algorithms and data structures to tackle complex problems. 

Main capabilities include detailed problem analyses (covering ideas, key points, and code implementations across simple, medium, and hard difficulties), structured data structure and algorithm summaries, anki flashcards for memorization, daily coding challenge archives, and a Chrome browser extension designed to enhance the practice workflow. Intended users are programmers and job seekers looking to systematically improve their coding interview performance. Notable technologies and formats utilized include Markdown documents, Anki packages, GitBook for online reading, and a custom Chrome extension.

name: dive-into-llms
description: 《动手学大模型Dive into LLMs》系列编程实践教程
summary:
《动手学大模型》系列编程实践教程是一个开源、免费的大模型入门编程参考项目，源自上海交通大学相关前沿技术与人工智能安全课程，并联合华为昇腾社区推出了国产化《大模型开发全流程》公益教程。

该项目旨在帮助学生、研究者和开发者快速掌握大模型应用与开发。其主要 capabilities 涵盖微调与部署、提示学习与思维链、知识编辑、数学推理、模型水印、越狱攻击、大模型隐写、多模态模型、GUI智能体、智能体安全以及基于PPO的RLHF安全对齐。

教程面向高校学生、AI研究者及广大开发者，提供配套的PPT课件、实验手册、视频及Jupyter Notebook脚本。项目重点应用了华为昇腾基础软硬件栈，支持昇腾生态中的模型迁移与调优实践。

name: PowerShell
description: PowerShell for every system!
summary:
PowerShell is a cross-platform (Windows, Linux, and macOS) automation and configuration tool and framework. It is optimized for handling structured data such as JSON, CSV, and XML, alongside REST APIs and object models. The project comprises a command-line shell, an associated scripting language, and a framework for processing cmdlets. 

Intended for administrators, developers, and engineers seeking system automation and configuration capabilities, the project supports building .NET Core C# applications targeting the PowerShell Core SDK NuGet package. Notable technologies include .NET Core, C#, and Docker containers, with the repository licensed under the MIT license.

name: Flowise
description: Build AI Agents, Visually
summary: Flowise is a tool designed to visually build AI agents. It features a mono repository architecture containing a Node backend server, a React frontend user interface, and third-party node integrations. The project provides quick start capabilities via npm and Docker support with Docker Compose. Developers can set up the environment using PNPM for package management. Flowise supports self-hosting across major cloud platforms including AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform, DigitalOcean, and Alibaba Cloud, alongside options like Railway, Render, HuggingFace Spaces, and Elestio.

name: Ghost
description: Independent technology for modern publishing, memberships, subscriptions and newsletters.
summary: Ghost is an open-source, headless Node.js content management system (CMS) designed for professional, independent publishing. It provides capabilities for content creation, API integration, custom theme development, and automated production deployment via an official command-line interface (ghost-cli) supporting local installations and server environments with automated SSL setup. Ghost targets publishers, developers, and content creators seeking a flexible publishing platform. The project is built using Node.js and relies on technologies such as a command-line interface, LetsEncrypt for SSL, and content APIs.

name: trackerslist
description: Updated list of public BitTorrent trackers
summary:
The `ngosang/trackerslist` repository provides automatically updated lists of public BitTorrent trackers. The project features multiple curated lists categorized by protocol and availability, including best trackers, all trackers, UDP, HTTP, HTTPS, WebSocket (WebTorrent), I2P, and Yggdrasil trackers, alongside DNS-independent lists using IP addresses instead of domains. An automated bot maintains these lists by checking tracker status, removing duplicates and Cloudflare-hosted IPs via a blacklist, and sorting entries by popularity and latency. 

The project is intended for BitTorrent users and developers seeking reliable, up-to-date tracker lists to improve torrent connectivity. It supports specialized networking technologies such as I2P routers and the Yggdrasil network, and integrates with third-party tools, scripts, and clients like qBittorrent, Transmission, Deluge, Aria2, and BiglyBT.

name: powerlevel10k
description: A Zsh theme
summary:
Powerlevel10k is a fast, highly customizable theme for Zsh that emphasizes performance and an out-of-the-box configuration experience through an interactive setup wizard (`p10k configure`). It supports instant prompt loading to eliminate Zsh startup lag, dynamic segment visibility ("show on command"), and transient prompt features. 

The project comes with dozens of built-in prompt segments displaying system, development, and repository information (such as Git status via the bundled `gitstatus` backend). It maintains full compatibility with Powerlevel9k configuration parameters and can emulate other themes like Pure.

Intended for Zsh users seeking a responsive and feature-rich prompt, Powerlevel10k performs optimally with Nerd Fonts (specifically recommending the patched MesloLGS NF font) and supports modern terminals with 256-color or truecolor capabilities.

name: gpt-engineer
description: CLI platform to experiment with codegen. Precursor to: https://lovable.dev
summary:
gpt-engineer is an open-source code generation experimentation platform and CLI tool designed for building software using artificial intelligence. Its primary purpose is to let users specify software requirements in natural language, watch an AI write and execute the code, and request iterative improvements. 

Main capabilities include generating new codebases, improving existing code via a `-i` flag, customizing AI behavior using overridable pre-prompts, supporting image inputs (such as UX or architecture diagrams) for vision-capable models, and benchmarking custom agent implementations against public datasets like APPS and MBPP using the included `bench` binary. 

The tool is intended for developers, coding agent builders, and researchers looking for a hackable CLI solution for AI-assisted software engineering. 

Notable technologies and integrations utilized include Python (supporting versions 3.10 through 3.12), Poetry for dependency management, Docker, GitHub Codespaces, and support for major AI model providers such as OpenAI API, Azure OpenAI API, and Anthropic, alongside open-source local models like WizardCoder.

name: awesome-claude-code
description: A hand-picked collection of the finest of resources for the most awesome of agents, Claude Code, the undisputed champion of coding companions, from the unstoppable team at Anthropic PBC. A delectable showcase of top tier skills, ambidextrous agents, scintillating status lines, top notch developer tooling, and also we have plugins
summary:
Awesome Claude Code is a hand-picked collection of resources, skills, plugins, developer tooling, and configuration guides for Claude Code, the coding companion developed by Anthropic. 

The project aims to provide beginners and veterans alike with practical extensions and frameworks focused on code quality, security, and originality. Its capabilities span documentation and learning materials, Obsidian-based knowledge graphs, scientific inquiry tools, runtime and integration infrastructure (such as browser automation and desktop bridges), remote control and voice I/O utilities, alternative clients and IDEs, status lines, design and UI/UX systems, writing and prose quality enhancers, creative media generators, DevOps automation, security guardrails, agent orchestration loops (including the "Ralph Wiggum" iterative technique), memory persistence, and observability dashboards. 

Notable technologies utilized across the listed resources include Rust, Python, TypeScript, Node.js, Swift, Go, Bun, Docker, Tauri, Obsidian, MCP (Model Context Protocol), Playwright, and OpenTelemetry.

name: freqtrade
description: Free, open source crypto trading bot
summary:
Freqtrade is a free and open-source cryptocurrency trading bot written in Python 3.11+. It is designed for crypto traders and developers seeking automated trading across major spot and futures exchanges such as Binance, Bybit, Kraken, OKX, and Hyperliquid. 

The platform provides comprehensive tools for backtesting, strategy optimization, data plotting, money management, and performance reporting. Notable capabilities include a risk-free dry-run mode, sqlite persistence, dynamic whitelisting and blacklisting, and FreqAI for adaptive machine learning prediction modeling and self-training strategies. Users can control and monitor the bot via a built-in WebUI, command-line interface, or Telegram integration. The project relies on technologies including Python, Docker, TA-Lib, and CCXT.

name: ImHex
description: 🔍 A Hex Editor for Reverse Engineers, Programmers and people who value their retinas when working at 3 AM.
summary:
ImHex is a feature-rich hex editor designed for reverse engineers, programmers, and security researchers. It provides comprehensive capabilities for inspecting, analyzing, and modifying binary data from various sources, including local files, raw disks, process memory, GDB servers, remote SFTP files, and UDP packets. 

Main capabilities include a flexible hex view with patching and search utilities, an integrated disassembler powered by Capstone, a node-based data pre-processor, extensive hashing and diffing support, YARA rule scanning, file entropy and type analysis, and a custom C++-like pattern language for parsing and visualizing file structures (such as images, audio, and 3D models). It also features a Data Inspector, bookmarks, customizable themes, a content updater for community patterns, and numerous built-in utilities like a calculator, demangler, and color picker.

ImHex targets developers and analysts on Windows, macOS, Linux, and FreeBSD, requiring a GPU with OpenGL 3.0 support or a software-rendered build mode. The project is built using C++23, utilizing GCC or LLVM Clang, and integrates libraries such as Dear ImGui, Capstone, and Yara.

name: segment-anything
description: The repository provides code for running inference with the SegmentAnything Model (SAM), links for downloading the trained model checkpoints, and example notebooks that show how to use the model.
summary:
The Segment Anything Model (SAM) and Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2) are foundational computer vision frameworks developed by Meta AI Research (FAIR) for promptable visual object segmentation across images and videos. SAM produces high-quality object masks from input prompts like points or boxes and supports automatic mask generation for entire images. SAM 2 extends this capability to real-time video processing using a transformer architecture with streaming memory. 

The project is intended for researchers, developers, and computer vision practitioners working on image and video segmentation tasks. It includes pre-trained model checkpoints in multiple backbone sizes (ViT-H, ViT-L, ViT-B), Python APIs (`SamPredictor`, `SamAutomaticMaskGenerator`, and `sam_model_registry`), command-line scripts, ONNX export capabilities for deployment in environments like web browsers, and a React-based web demo. The models are trained on large-scale datasets including the SA-1B dataset and the SA-V video segmentation dataset.

Notable technologies used include Python, PyTorch, TorchVision, OpenCV, ONNX Runtime, and Pycocotools.

name: goose
description: an open source, extensible AI agent that goes beyond code suggestions - install, execute, edit, and test with any LLM
summary:
Goose is a native open-source general-purpose AI agent designed to run locally for tasks including coding, research, writing, automation, and data analysis. It is available as a native desktop application for macOS, Linux, and Windows, a full command-line interface (CLI) for terminal workflows, and an API for embedding. Built in Rust for performance and portability, the project is part of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) at the Linux Foundation.

Goose integrates with over 15 AI providers—such as Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama, OpenRouter, Azure, and Amazon Bedrock—allowing users to utilize direct API keys or existing ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini subscriptions via ACP. Additionally, it connects to more than 70 extensions through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) open standard.

name: odoo
description: Odoo. Open Source Apps To Grow Your Business.
summary: Odoo is a suite of web-based, open-source business applications that can function as stand-alone tools or integrate seamlessly to form a full-featured open-source ERP. The primary applications include an open-source CRM, Website Builder, eCommerce, Warehouse Management, Project Management, Billing & Accounting, Point of Sale, Human Resources, Marketing, and Manufacturing. The repository is intended for businesses, administrators, and developers looking to deploy, learn, or extend enterprise management software.

name: dive
description: A tool for exploring each layer in a docker image
summary: Dive is a command-line tool designed for exploring Docker and OCI images, inspecting layer contents, and discovering ways to reduce image size. Its main capabilities include breaking down image contents by layer, indicating file changes (additions, modifications, and removals), estimating image efficiency and wasted space, and providing quick build-and-analysis cycles. Additionally, Dive supports CI pipeline integration to evaluate images against efficiency and wasted space metrics, returning pass/fail results based on configured thresholds. The tool supports multiple image sources and container engines, including Docker, Docker tar archives, and Podman. Dive is intended for developers, container administrators, and CI/CD engineers looking to optimize container image sizes. It is built using Go.

name: VibeVoice
description: Open-Source Frontier Voice AI
summary:
VibeVoice is an open-source framework of frontier voice AI models comprising both Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Text-to-Speech (TTS) capabilities. Designed for researchers and developers, the project focuses on handling long-form audio sequences efficiently through ultra-low frame rate (7.5 Hz) continuous acoustic and semantic speech tokenizers combined with a next-token diffusion framework and Large Language Models (LLMs).

Main capabilities include:
- **VibeVoice-ASR:** A 7B parameter unified speech-to-text model capable of processing up to 60-minute long-form audio in a single pass. It outputs structured transcriptions containing speaker identity, timestamps, and content, supporting customized hotwords, streaming recognition across 10+ languages, vLLM acceleration, and CPU edge inference via heterogeneous quantization (VibeVoice-ASR-BitNet).
- **VibeVoice-TTS & Realtime-0.5B:** Long-form and real-time text-to-speech models supporting multi-speaker dialogues (up to 4 speakers) and generation lengths up to 90 minutes with streaming text inputs.

Technologies utilized include continuous speech tokenizers, diffusion heads, Qwen2.5 base models, vLLM, and BitNet-based CPU quantization (I8_S + I2_S).

name: ChatGPT
description: ❄️ ChatGPT Desktop Application (Mac, Windows and Linux)
summary: The ChatGPT Desktop Application is a cross-platform desktop wrapper for ChatGPT available on Mac, Windows, and Linux. Developed as a precursor concept to the Noi application, the project aims to provide a dedicated desktop experience for interacting with ChatGPT outside of a standard web browser.

name: core
description: 🖖 Vue.js is a progressive, incrementally-adoptable JavaScript framework for building UI on the web.
summary: Vue.js (`vuejs/core`) is the official repository for the Vue.js progressive JavaScript framework core, distributed under an MIT license. It provides an open-source framework designed for building user interfaces and web applications. The project targets developers seeking a flexible, component-based approach to frontend development. Detailed documentation, getting started guides, and community support channels are available through vuejs.org, the official forum, and community chat.

name: requests
description: A simple, yet elegant, HTTP library.
summary:
Requests is a simple and elegant HTTP library for Python designed to send HTTP/1.1 requests easily without manually formatting query strings or form-encoded data. Intended for developers building robust and reliable HTTP-speaking applications, it supports Python 3.10+. 

Main capabilities include Keep-Alive and connection pooling, international domains and URLs, sessions with cookie persistence, browser-style TLS/SSL verification, Basic and Digest authentication, dictionary-like cookies, automatic content decompression and decoding, multi-part file uploads, SOCKS proxy support, connection timeouts, streaming downloads, automatic honoring of `.netrc`, and chunked HTTP requests.

name: maybe
description: The personal finance app for everyone
summary: Maybe is a fully working personal finance application designed for self-hosting via Docker and local development. It provides users with personal finance tracking capabilities. Intended for individuals wanting to self-host their financial data and developers contributing to the codebase, the project requires Ruby and PostgreSQL. Notable technologies used include Docker, Ruby, and PostgreSQL. The repository is distributed under the AGPLv3 license and is no longer actively maintained.

name: FlClash
description: A multi-platform proxy client based on ClashMeta,simple and easy to use, open-source and ad-free.
summary:
FlClash is an open-source, ad-free multi-platform proxy client based on the ClashMeta (mihomo) core. It is built using Flutter, Go, and Rust, and is designed for users across Android, Windows, macOS, and Linux. 

The project provides comprehensive proxy capabilities, including rule routing, proxy groups, latency testing, system proxy settings, and TUN mode. Users can manage profiles via subscription links or local files, utilizing built-in editors, override scripts, and custom rules. FlClash also offers live monitoring of connections, requests, DNS queries, and logs, alongside data backup and restoration through WebDAV or local storage. 

Designed with a Material You interface featuring dynamic colors and adaptive layouts, the application integrates platform-specific functionalities such as Quick Settings tiles, per-app proxy routing, and Android TV support on Android, as well as tray menus and global hotkeys on desktop environments.

name: lx-music-desktop
description: 一个基于 Electron 的音乐软件
summary: LX Music 桌面版是一个基于 Electron 和 Vue 开发的音乐软件，支持 Linux、macOS 以及 Windows 7 及以上平台。该项目旨在提供一个跨平台的桌面音乐播放体验，具备 Scheme URL 支持、独立数据同步服务支持以及开放 API 服务能力，允许本地启动 HTTP 服务供第三方调用。默认设置不以新手友好为目标，提供灵活的配置、鼠标与键盘快捷操作以及播放列表机制。开发者建议日常使用者未来迁移至新项目 Any Listen。本项目采用 Apache License 2.0 许可证发行。

name: whisper.cpp
description: Port of OpenAI's Whisper model in C/C++
summary:
whisper.cpp provides high-performance, plain C/C++ inference for OpenAI's Whisper automatic speech recognition (ASR) model without runtime memory allocations. It utilizes the `ggml` machine learning library to support mixed F16/F32 precision, integer quantization, and CPU-only or hardware-accelerated inference across platforms including macOS, iOS, Android, Linux, Windows, WebAssembly, and Docker. 

Hardware acceleration capabilities include Apple Silicon (via ARM NEON, Accelerate framework, Metal, Core ML, and ANEForge), NVIDIA GPUs (via CUDA and cuBLAS), AMD ROCm, Vulkan, OpenVINO, AMD Ryzen AI NPUs, Ascend NPUs, Moore Threads GPUs, POWER VSX, and OpenBLAS CPU acceleration. The project also incorporates Voice Activity Detection (VAD) using models like Silero-VAD, and provides a C-style API alongside numerous bindings for languages such as Rust, JavaScript, Go, Java, Python, C#, and Swift. Intended users include developers seeking to integrate offline speech-to-text transcription, voice assistants, and real-time audio processing into local applications, mobile devices, and web servers.

name: material-design-icons
description: Material Design icons by Google (Material Symbols)
summary:
This repository contains two official icon sets from Google designed under the Material Design guidelines: Material Symbols and Material Icons. 

Material Symbols is the current, actively updated set built on variable font technology and available in Outlined, Rounded, and Sharp styles. It features adjustable design axes including Optical Size, Weight, Grade, and Fill. Material Icons is the classic, legacy set (updates halted in 2022) available in five styles: Outlined, Filled, Rounded, Sharp, and Two Tone. 

The project is intended for designers and developers looking to incorporate official Google Material design icons into web, Android, and iOS products. 

Notable technologies and formats used include WOFF2 and WOFF variable fonts, static font files, CSS, Sass, SVG, and Android/iOS asset directories.

name: element
description: A Vue.js 2.0 UI Toolkit for Web
summary: Element (Element UI) is a Vue.js 2.0 UI toolkit for the web, designed for developers building web applications using Vue.js 2.x. It provides a comprehensive set of components and theme customization capabilities, supporting modern browsers as well as Internet Explorer 10+. Notable technologies used include Vue.js and CSS (specifically via the theme-chalk theme and custom theme generation tools).

name: CLIProxyAPI
description: Wrap Antigravity, ChatGPT Codex, Claude Code, Grok Build, Muse Code, Devin as an OpenAI/Gemini/Claude/Codex compatible API service, allowing you to enjoy the free Gemini Series, GPT Series, Grok Series, Claude model through API
summary:
CLIProxyAPI is a proxy server designed to provide OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, Codex, Grok, Kimi, and Meta-compatible API interfaces for command-line interfaces and clients. It allows developers and users to access multiple CLI accounts locally through any compatible client or SDK using OAuth logins and API keys.

Main capabilities include support for streaming, non-streaming, and WebSocket responses, function calling, tools, multimodal inputs (text and images), and round-robin load balancing across multiple accounts for Gemini, OpenAI, Claude, and Grok. It also features simple CLI authentication flows, generative language API key support, and a reusable Go SDK for embedding the proxy.

Intended users include developers and software engineers seeking unified, multi-account AI model access and load balancing for coding assistants and automation workflows. Notable technologies utilized include Go, OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, OAuth, and various model endpoints such as OpenAI GPT, Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, xAI Grok, Moonshot AI Kimi, and Meta Muse.

name: pdf.js
description: PDF Reader in JavaScript
summary:
PDF.js is a community-driven, Mozilla-supported open-source project that provides a general-purpose, web standards-based platform for parsing and rendering Portable Document Format (PDF) files using HTML5. 

Its main capabilities include a web-based PDF viewer, a built-in PDF debugger to examine internal document structures, and JavaScript APIs for integrating PDF viewing and interaction into web applications. It can be used via pre-built NPM packages (such as `pdfjs-dist`), public CDNs, or browser extensions for Firefox and Chrome. 

The project is intended for web developers, end-users, and contributors seeking to render or manipulate PDF documents natively within web browsers. Notable technologies and tools used in the project include HTML5, JavaScript, Node.js, Gulp, Babel, and Puppeteer.

name: fanqiang
description: 翻墙-科学上网
summary:
This repository is a comprehensive project and tutorial library for bypassing internet censorship, providing scientific internet access (fanqiang) tools and configurations across multiple platforms. 

**Main Capabilities:**
*   **One-Click Proxy Packages:** Provides out-of-the-box browser integration kits such as ChromeGo, EdgeGo, and Firefox packages for Windows, Mac, and Linux, bundled with built-in free servers.
*   **Client Configuration Tutorials:** Guides users through setting up popular proxy clients and apps including Clash (Clash for Windows, ClashX, Clash for Android), V2rayN, V2RayNG, Shadowrocket, Quantumult X, Surge, SSTap, Netch, and TorBrowser.
*   **Server Deployment:** Offers concise guides for self-hosting V2ray and Shadowsocks servers, alongside free account resources.
*   **Multi-Platform Support:** Details instructions for Windows, macOS, iOS (iPhone/iPad), Android, Linux, routers (OpenWRT, Merlin), game consoles (PS4, PS5, Switch, Xbox), and Apple TV.
*   **Specific Services:** Includes guides for registering for ChatGPT from mainland China and configuring chained proxies.

**Notable Technologies:**
V2ray, Shadowsocks (SS), ShadowsocksR (SSR), Clash, Goflyway, Daze, Brook, Lightsocks, Trojan, Psiphon, and Lantern.

name: humanizer
description: Agent skill that removes signs of AI-generated writing from text
summary:
Humanizer is an open-source tool designed to rewrite AI-generated text so that it reads naturally as if written by a person, without altering its core meaning. Built upon Wikipedia's guidelines for identifying AI writing ("Signs of AI writing"), it detects and corrects 26 distinct writing patterns—such as forced triads, dramatic one-line closers, overused AI vocabulary, and staged transitions. 

The project functions as an agent skill integrated into environments like Claude Code, Codex, the Skills CLI (supporting Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, and Windsurf), and Claude Desktop. Intended users include writers, developers, and professionals seeking to remove artificial tropes and stylistic boilerplate from their prose. Humanizer supports voice matching via user writing samples, preserves factual accuracy by avoiding unsupported fabrications, and leaves surrounding elements like code and data untouched when editing files. It is licensed under the MIT License.

name: BMAD-METHOD
description: Breakthrough Method for Agile Ai Driven Development
summary:
BMad Method is an Agile AI-Driven Development (AiDD) framework designed to turn ideas or change requests into working software while keeping human judgment central. It covers the entire delivery lifecycle—from clarifying and planning to building, verifying, and learning—scaling its process depth to match the complexity of the work, whether for weekend prototypes or long-standing systems. 

The project aims to keep product, architectural, and technical decisions explicit, carrying durable context forward across sessions instead of relying on re-explained chat prompts. It supports both new projects and inherited codebases, offering specialized perspectives in product, architecture, UX, development, and testing.

Intended for developers and teams using AI coding tools, BMad integrates via tools supporting skills and Python's `uv`, including a Skills CLI (using Node.js, npm, and Git) and plugins for Claude Code and Codex. Technologies utilized include Python, Node.js, Git, and a modular ecosystem featuring extensions like the BMad Builder, BMad Test Architect, BMad Loop, and BMad Game Dev Studio. BMad is licensed under the MIT License.

name: chinese-poetry
description: The most comprehensive database of Chinese poetry 🧶最全中华古诗词数据库,  唐宋两朝近一万四千古诗人,  接近5.5万首唐诗加26万宋诗.  两宋时期1564位词人，21050首词。
summary:
The `chinese-poetry` repository provides a comprehensive open-source database of classical Chinese poetry and literature distributed in JSON format. Its primary purpose is to preserve and promote classical Chinese literature by making texts easily accessible for developers to build poetry-related applications, websites, and machine learning models. 

The database includes over 55,000 Tang poems, 260,000 Song poems, 21,000 Song lyrics (Ci), and covers nearly 14,000 poets from the Tang and Song dynasties alongside 1,500 lyricists. Additional collections comprise the *Book of Songs* (*Shi Jing*), *Analects* (*Lun Yu*), *Huajian Ji*, *Nantang Er Zhu Ci*, the *Four Books and Five Classics*, *Mengxue* texts, works by Nalan Xingde, and comprehensive imperial editions like *Yuding Quan Tang Shi*.

Intended users include developers, researchers, and educators building software such as mobile apps, web interfaces, desktop tools, and deep learning text generation models. Notable technologies and integrations associated with downstream use cases include PyTorch, PaddlePaddle, RNN models, Transformer-based architectures like ERNIE-GEN, Android, MySQL, and WeChat mini-programs. The project is licensed under the MIT License and accepts community contributions via pull requests and issue discussions.

name: awesome-ios
description: A curated list of awesome iOS ecosystem, including Objective-C and Swift Projects
summary: Awesome iOS is a curated list of open-source frameworks, libraries, tools, and resources for iOS development. The repository aggregates thousands of packages and utilities categorized by domain, including analytics, app routing, architecture patterns (such as VIPER, MVVM, and Clean Architecture), ARKit, authentication, blockchain, caching, charts, code quality, concurrency, core data, databases, data structures, networking, UI components, testing tools, and more. It serves as a comprehensive reference guide for iOS developers, engineers, and students seeking pre-built solutions and learning materials implemented primarily in Swift and Objective-C.

name: normalize.css
description: A modern alternative to CSS resets
summary:
normalize.css is a modern CSS reset alternative designed for web developers and designers. Its project purpose is to make browsers render all elements more consistently and in line with modern standards. 

Main capabilities include preserving useful defaults instead of erasing them, normalizing styles for a wide range of HTML elements, correcting common browser bugs and inconsistencies, improving usability via subtle modifications, and providing detailed comments explaining the code. It targets web developers and supports browsers including Chrome, Edge, Firefox ESR+, Internet Explorer 10+, Safari 8+, and Opera. Notable technologies include CSS, NPM, and CDNs.

name: kotlin
description: The Kotlin Programming Language.
summary:
Kotlin is a concise, multiplatform programming language developed by JetBrains and contributors. Designed for software developers, it features robust multiplatform capabilities—including Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform—enabling the sharing of business logic and user interfaces across Android, iOS, desktop, and web environments while retaining native programming flexibility. 

The repository provides the complete source code, standard library, and compiler for the language. Notable technologies and tools utilized in the project include Gradle (leveraging toolchains and dependency verification features), Eclipse Adoptium for JDK provisioning, Maven Central for publishing artifacts, and integration support for development environments like IntelliJ IDEA and Eclipse. The project is distributed under the Apache License 2.0.

name: windows
description: Windows inside a Docker container.
summary:
dockur/windows runs Microsoft Windows inside a Docker or Podman container with near-native performance using KVM acceleration. Designed for developers, system administrators, and home lab users, the project supports modern and legacy Windows releases (including Windows 7 through 11, Windows Server editions, and Tiny variants), as well as custom ISO images and ReactOS. 

Main capabilities include automatic download and hands-free installation, customizable CPU, RAM, and disk storage allocation, dynamic memory allocation via memory ballooning, USB passthrough, and host folder sharing. It supports diverse networking setups such as NAT, user-mode, macvlan, and macvtap, with options for DHCP and Active Directory domain joining. Users can interact with the container via a web browser-based viewer or Microsoft Remote Desktop (RDP). 

Notable technologies used include Docker, Podman, Kubernetes, QEMU, and KVM.

name: Fooocus
description: Focus on prompting and generating
summary:
Fooocus is an offline, open-source, and free image-generating software built on the Stable Diffusion XL architecture and utilizing Gradio. It is designed to combine the high-quality text-to-image capabilities and ease of use found in online tools like Midjourney with offline software control, requiring no manual parameter tweaking or extensive prompt engineering. 

The software's main capabilities include text-to-image generation powered by an offline GPT-2 based prompt processing engine, as well as built-in support for upscaling, variations, inpainting, outpainting, image prompts, FaceSwap, and style management. Notable technical features encompass native refiner swapping within a single k-sampler, negative ADM guidance, and Self-Attention Guidance to prevent overly smooth or plastic image generation. 

Fooocus is intended for users seeking high-quality image generation locally with minimal setup. It requires a minimum of 4GB of Nvidia GPU memory (VRAM) or equivalent hardware acceleration via AMD or Apple silicon, along with at least 8GB of system memory and system swap.

name: i-have-adhd
description: A skill to stop your coding agent from burying the answer. ADHD-friendly output.
summary:
i-have-adhd is a skill and plugin for coding assistants designed to provide ADHD-friendly outputs by eliminating conversational preamble, recaps, and filler phrases, and instead prioritizing direct, action-first responses. 

Project capabilities include leading with immediate actions, numbering multi-step tasks, ending with single concrete next steps, suppressing tangents, restating state every turn, giving specific time estimates, making wins visible, keeping error messages matter-of-fact, capping lists to five items, and removing boilerplate closers like "Hope this helps!". The rules are fully defined in an editable markdown file (`SKILL.md`).

The project is intended for users of AI coding assistants who prefer concise, structured, and straightforward technical answers. Technologies mentioned include CLI installations, `npm`, and integration plugins for tools such as Claude (`claude plugin`).

name: claude-cookbooks
description: A collection of notebooks/recipes showcasing some fun and effective ways of using Claude.
summary:
Claude Cookbooks is a developer-focused repository providing guides and copyable code snippets to help build applications with the Claude API from Anthropic. Primarily written in Python, the project offers practical examples across several categories, including text and data classification, retrieval augmented generation (RAG), summarization, and multimodal capabilities like vision processing, chart interpretation, and form data extraction. 

The repository demonstrates tool use and integrations with external systems such as calculators, SQL queries, Pinecone vector databases, Wikipedia, web pages, and Voyage AI embeddings. It also covers advanced techniques including sub-agents (combining Haiku and Opus models), PDF parsing, automated prompt evaluations, JSON mode, content moderation filters, prompt caching, and cost optimization strategies. Intended for developers looking to integrate Claude into software projects, the recipes require a Claude API key and can be adapted to any programming language capable of interacting with the API.

name: lazydocker
description: The lazier way to manage everything docker
summary:
Lazydocker is a simple terminal UI designed for managing Docker and Docker-Compose environments. Written in Go using the gocui library, the project aims to reduce the friction of working with CLI commands by placing all container states, logs, metrics graphs, and management actions within a single interactive terminal window. 

Main capabilities include:
- Viewing the overall state of Docker or Docker-Compose container environments at a glance.
- Monitoring and streaming container or service logs.
- Visualizing container metrics using ASCII graphs with customizable measurements.
- Attaching to containers or services.
- Performing lifecycle operations such as restarting, removing, rebuilding, and pruning containers, images, or volumes.
- Exploring ancestor layers of Docker images.
- Supporting both keyboard navigation and mouse interactions.

The project is intended for developers and system administrators who work frequently with Docker and seek a lightweight, keyboard-driven terminal dashboard for day-to-day container management. Notable technologies used in its development include Go, Docker, Docker-Compose, and the gocui terminal user interface library.

name: Docker-OSX
description: Run macOS VM in a Docker! Run near native OSX-KVM in Docker! X11 Forwarding! CI/CD for OS X Security Research! Docker mac Containers.
summary:
Docker-OSX is a tool designed to run Apple Mac OS X and macOS virtual machines inside Docker containers with near-native performance using QEMU and KVM. It is built for security research, application testing, and CI/CD pipelines, supporting versions ranging from Mac OS X High Sierra up to newer releases like Sonoma, Sequoia, and Tahoe.

Main capabilities include X11 forwarding, VNC and SPICE headless display options, SSH access, folder and disk sharing via QEMU and NFS, USB passthrough, and iPhone/iPad USB-to-network passthrough using `usbfluxd`. It also provides automated and manual serial number generation to support features requiring Apple services like iMessage and iCloud.

The project is primarily intended for security researchers, developers, and power users running Linux or Windows hosts via Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL2). Notable underlying technologies include Docker, QEMU, KVM, OpenCore, and libvirt.

name: awesome-openclaw-skills
description: The awesome collection of OpenClaw skills. 5,400+ skills filtered and categorized from the official OpenClaw Skills Registry.🦞
summary:
Awesome OpenClaw Skills is a curated repository of over 5,300 community-built skills for OpenClaw, a locally running AI assistant that operates directly on users' machines. The project aims to help users discover, evaluate, and install extensions that enable OpenClaw to interact with external services, automate workflows, and perform specialized tasks. 

Categorized across diverse domains—including coding agents and IDEs, web and frontend development, browser automation, DevOps and cloud, search and research, marketing and sales, productivity, notes and personal knowledge management, communication, and self-hosted automation—the collection features skills sourced from ClawHub, OpenClaw's public skills registry. It also highlights ecosystem tools for web crawling, search APIs, and managed AI hosting.

Intended for developers and users of OpenClaw looking to expand their assistant's capabilities, the repository provides installation guides supporting the OpenClaw CLI, ClawHub CLI, manual placement, and chat-based link pasting. Notable technologies and integrations referenced include OpenClaw, ClawHub, Git, GitHub, Python, Swift, SQLite, and various third-party APIs.

name: chrome-devtools-mcp
description: Chrome DevTools for coding agents
summary:
`chrome-devtools-mcp` (Chrome DevTools for agents) is a Model-Context-Protocol (MCP) server and CLI tool that enables coding agents and AI assistants—such as Antigravity, Claude, Cursor, and Copilot—to control and inspect a live Google Chrome or Chrome for Testing browser. 

The project's main capabilities include reliable browser automation, advanced debugging, network request analysis, screenshot capture, console message inspection with source-mapped stack traces, and recording performance traces to extract actionable insights using Chrome DevTools frontend and Puppeteer. It is intended for developers and coding agents requiring deep browser integration for testing, debugging, and performance analysis. Notable technologies used include Node.js, npm, Puppeteer, and the Chrome DevTools frontend and Google CrUX API.

name: ionic-framework
description: A powerful cross-platform UI toolkit for building native-quality iOS, Android, and Progressive Web Apps with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
summary: Ionic is an open-source app development toolkit designed for building cross-platform native and Progressive Web Apps from a single codebase using JavaScript and the web. Based on Web Components, Ionic provides performance, usability, and feature improvements while offering support for popular web frameworks including Angular, React, and Vue. The project comprises core packages such as `@ionic/core`, `@ionic/angular`, `@ionic/vue`, and `@ionic/react`.

name: marketingskills
description: Marketing skills for Claude Code and AI agents. CRO, copywriting, SEO, analytics, and growth engineering.
summary:
Marketing Skills for AI Agents is an open-source library of markdown-based agent skills designed to provide AI coding assistants with specialized knowledge and workflows for marketing tasks. Created for technical marketers and founders, the project helps AI agents execute conversion rate optimization (CRO), copywriting, search engine optimization (SEO), analytics, paid advertising, and growth engineering. 

The collection functions across AI agents that support the Agent Skills specification, including Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, and Windsurf. It builds upon a foundational `product-marketing` skill and connects a wide ecosystem of sub-skills covering categories such as conversion optimization, content and copy, SEO and discovery, paid acquisition, measurement, retention, growth engineering, strategy, monetization, and revenue operations (RevOps). 

Users can install the repository as a CLI tool via `npx skills`, through agent-specific plugin systems (such as Claude Code or OpenAI Codex), or by cloning, forking, or adding it as a Git submodule. The project is distributed under the MIT license.

name: expo
description: An open-source framework for making universal native apps with React. Expo runs on Android, iOS, and the web.
summary:
Expo is an open-source platform designed for building universal native applications that run on Android, iOS, and the web. It provides a universal runtime and a comprehensive suite of libraries allowing developers to construct native apps using React and JavaScript. 

The repository contains core components such as the Expo SDK, Modules API, the Expo Go app, CLI, Expo Router, documentation, and various supporting tools and templates. It integrates with Expo Application Services (EAS), a hosted platform for building, shipping, and managing apps. The project is intended for individual developers and teams building cross-platform applications and custom native modules. Notable technologies referenced include React, React Native, JavaScript, Android, iOS, and web platforms.

name: VoiceStudio
description: VoiceStudio is the open-source, fully-local ElevenLabs alternative — voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription & audiobook creation in 646 languages.
summary:
VoiceStudio is an open-source desktop application and web UI designed for local voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription, and audiobook creation supporting 646 languages. 

Key capabilities include voice cloning via clean reference recordings, custom voice design, timed speech video dubbing, a floating dictation widget, batch jobs, local model management, and local API and Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations for AI agents. The default engine is powered by k2-fsa/OmniVoice, with options for other speech engines and optional remote workers.

The project is intended for users seeking local text-to-speech, transcription, and dubbing workflows that run on their own hardware, including support for NVIDIA GPU CUDA acceleration, Apple Silicon Metal (MPS), and CPU execution. 

Notable technologies used in the stack include Electron, Node.js, Bun, Rust/Cargo, Python, and PyTorch. The application is distributed under the AGPL-3.0 license.

name: open-source-ios-apps
description: :iphone: Collaborative List of Open-Source iOS Apps
summary:
This repository maintains a collaborative, curated directory of open-source applications built for Apple ecosystems, spanning iOS, iPadOS, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS. Its purpose is to catalog real-world applications and codebases across diverse categories such as productivity, tools, utilities, developer resources, communication, finance, health, media, games, and security. 

Intended for developers, learners, and enthusiasts, the list serves as a resource for exploring complete project architectures, code examples, and design patterns. It highlights applications built with prominent native frameworks—including Swift, SwiftUI, Objective-C, Core Data, WidgetKit, RealityKit, and ARKit—alongside cross-platform technologies like Flutter, React Native, and Kotlin Multiplatform.

name: llama_index
description: LlamaIndex is the document processing platform for AI
summary:
LlamaIndex Framework is an open-source data framework designed to help developers build LLM applications, RAG pipelines, and agentic workflows by augmenting large language models with private data. 

**Main Capabilities:**
- Ingests data from diverse sources and formats (such as APIs, PDFs, documents, and SQL) via data connectors.
- Structures data into indices and graphs for efficient use with LLMs.
- Provides advanced retrieval and query interfaces alongside modular lower-level APIs for customization.
- Features LlamaParse for document parsing, agentic OCR, and structured data extraction.

**Intended Users:**
Developers, AI startups, and enterprises looking to build LLM apps, automate document workflows, and integrate custom data sources with language models.

**Notable Technologies:**
Python, OpenAI, Ollama, HuggingFace, and LlamaIndex core/integration packages.

name: cherry-studio
description: AI productivity studio with smart chat, autonomous agents, and 300+ assistants. Unified access to frontier LLMs
summary:
Cherry Studio is a cross-platform desktop client designed for Windows, Mac, and Linux that supports multiple Large Language Model (LLM) providers and AI web services such as OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, Claude, Perplexity, Poe, Ollama, and LM Studio. 

Intended for individual users, developers, and enterprises, the project features over 300 pre-configured AI assistants, custom assistant creation, multi-model simultaneous conversations, and support for text, image, Office, and PDF document processing. Notable capabilities include WebDAV file management, Mermaid chart visualization, code syntax highlighting, global search, topic management, AI-powered translation, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server integration. 

Technologies and protocols used include Electron-based cross-platform UI, Ollama, LM Studio, WebDAV, and MCP. An Enterprise Edition is also available, providing centralized model and employee management, enterprise-grade knowledge bases, role-based access control, and private on-premises deployment options.

name: hiring-without-whiteboards
description: ⭐️  Companies that don't have a broken hiring process
summary:
Hiring Without Whiteboards is a curated, community-driven list of companies and teams that reject traditional whiteboard and computer science trivia interviews in favor of practical assessment methods. Designed for software engineers, developers, and technical job seekers, the repository aims to promote hiring practices that reflect day-to-day work. 

The project highlights alternative evaluation techniques utilized by listed organizations, such as pairing on real-world problems, conducting code reviews, reviewing open-source contributions, and completing paid or unpaid take-home exercises. Rather than testing abstract algorithms, riddles, or brainteasers using platforms like LeetCode or HackerRank, the featured companies focus on practical problem-solving, architectural discussions, system design, and team collaboration. 

The repository provides a structured directory categorized alphabetically, detailing specific interview workflows for hundreds of global companies and remote teams, alongside recommendations for conducting better engineering interviews.

name: etcd
description: Distributed reliable key-value store for the most critical data of a distributed system
summary: etcd is a distributed, reliable key-value store designed to manage critical data for distributed systems. Its core capabilities include high availability via the Raft consensus algorithm, a well-defined gRPC user-facing API, and automatic TLS security with optional client certificate authentication. Written in Go, it features command-line client tooling via `etcdctl` and supports robust, replicated logging. The project is intended for developers and operators building critical distributed deployments and is frequently integrated with applications such as Kubernetes, locksmith, vulcand, and Doorman.

name: prettier
description: Prettier is an opinionated code formatter.
summary:
Prettier is an opinionated code formatter designed to enforce a consistent coding style across a codebase. It works by parsing source code and re-printing it according to built-in rules that respect maximum line lengths and wrap code when necessary. 

The tool supports a wide range of languages and formats, including JavaScript, TypeScript, Flow, JSX, JSON, CSS, SCSS, Less, HTML, Vue, Angular, GraphQL, Markdown, and YAML, with support for additional plugins. 

Intended for developers and teams seeking automated code formatting, Prettier can be integrated directly into code editors for on-save formatting, incorporated into pre-commit hooks, or executed within CI environments.

name: grok-1
description: Grok open release
summary:
Grok-1 provides JAX example code for loading and running the Grok-1 open-weights large language model. The project purpose is to enable users to download model checkpoints and run sampling tests on input data. The repository targets developers and researchers working with large-scale machine learning models who possess hardware with sufficient GPU memory. 

Notable technologies and specifications include an Apache 2.0 license, JAX for execution, a SentencePiece tokenizer supporting 131,072 tokens, and a Mixture of 8 Experts (MoE) architecture comprising 314 billion parameters, 64 layers, 48 query attention heads, 8 key/value attention heads, a 6,144 embedding size, and an 8,192 token maximum sequence length. The model incorporates rotary embeddings (RoPE), activation sharding, and 8-bit quantization. The repository includes an unoptimized MoE layer implementation designed to validate correctness without custom kernels.

name: ai-agent-book
description: 《深入理解 AI Agent：设计原理与工程实践》（李博杰 著）开源主仓库：全书正文、编译版 PDF 与按章配套代码
summary:
The repository "深入理解 AI Agent：设计原理与工程实践" (Understanding AI Agents: Design Principles and Engineering Practices) is an open-source book and companion project covering the design principles and engineering implementation of AI agents from fundamentals to production. 

Based on the core formula **Agent = LLM + Context + Tools**, the project spans 10 chapters addressing topics such as context engineering, user memory and knowledge bases, tools and the MCP protocol, coding agents, multimodal and interactive observation/action spaces, model evaluation, model post-training (SFT and RL), continuous evolution, and multi-agent collaboration. 

Main capabilities include 109 open-source companion experiments, offline and online multi-language reading across 15 languages (including PDF and EPUB formats), and support for Python 3.11–3.13 environments using `uv` and `pip`. 

The intended users are developers, engineers, and researchers seeking to build, evaluate, and scale LLM-based applications and AI agents. Notable technologies and frameworks referenced include LLMs, KV Cache, RAG, MCP (Model Context Protocol), Computer Use, VLLM, Unsloth, and custom training stacks.

name: dbeaver
description: Free universal database tool and SQL client
summary:
DBeaver is a free, multi-platform database management tool and universal client designed for developers, SQL programmers, database administrators, and analysts. It provides comprehensive capabilities including a schema editor, SQL editor, data editor, Entity-Relationship (ER) diagrams, data export, import, and migration tools, SQL execution plans, database administration tools, dashboards, a spatial data viewer, proxy and SSH tunnelling, and a custom database drivers editor. It supports over 100 database drivers out of the box and can connect to virtually any database utilizing a JDBC or ODBC driver. Additionally, DBeaver integrates AI-powered tools for generating, analyzing, and optimizing SQL queries and interacting with database structures. 

The application is written primarily in Java and built using the OSGi platform for plugin and dependency management, the Eclipse Rich Client Platform (RCP) for its desktop user interface, and JDBC for database connectivity. It incorporates parsers like JSQLParser and ANTLR4, alongside libraries such as SSHJ, Apache POI, JFreeChart, and JTS.

name: guava
description: Google core libraries for Java
summary:
Guava is a set of core Java libraries from Google designed to provide foundational utilities for Java projects. Its main capabilities include new collection types such as multimap and multiset, immutable collections, a graph library, and utilities for concurrency, I/O, hashing, primitives, and strings. 

Intended for Java developers and Android developers, Guava is distributed in two separate flavors: a JRE flavor requiring JDK 1.8 or higher, and an Android flavor compatible with Android environments. Notable technologies and build tools supported include Maven and Gradle.

name: multica
description: Make humans and AI agents work as one team — open-source and self-hostable.
summary:
Multica is a source-available workspace that integrates AI coding agents and human teammates onto a single project board. Users assign issues directly to AI agents—such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Kimi, Grok, and over 20 other supported agent CLIs—which independently pick up tasks, execute them on local or cloud runtimes, provide execution logs, and return completed work for human review. 

Designed for development teams, Multica supports collaborative squads, reusable agent skills, autopilots, projects, and custom review gates. The platform ensures code stays securely on local machines or user-managed infrastructure via a local daemon architecture. It features self-hosting capabilities using Docker Compose or Helm, integrations with Git hosts like GitHub and GitLab, and messaging channels including Slack, Telegram, and Feishu. 

The technology stack utilizes Next.js 16 for the web interface, Electron for the desktop application, Expo and React Native for mobile apps, a Go backend using the Chi router and WebSockets, and PostgreSQL 17 for the database.

name: 100-Days-Of-ML-Code
description: 100 Days of ML Coding
summary:
The 100-Days-Of-ML-Code repository documents a 100-day journey of learning and coding machine learning concepts, originally proposed by Siraj Raval.
